Do not commit anything in the main tree; leave both files uncommitted.

## The owner's request (2026-11-20)
"As for displaying the notifications in an alternative manner, what other sorts of things could we use in displaying here? I would like for you to examine my current research on Glamorous Toolkit, as well as other UI libraries, to see what sort of language we can use to convey notifications in another manner that perhaps is better than simple text."
Context: Farhan delays notifications by priority (Critical immediate; High, Medium, Low on cadences) under a points budget. Its Inbox lists notifications as text rows (app name, title, text, time) with priority chips; the Notification dashboard has widgets (priority distribution, top chatters, category breakdown, budget spend, standing alarms, flood status, recent batches). The owner already chose a bottom bar (Overview / Inbox / Apps) for that area; do not redesign navigation. Current screens: notification_filter/notification_filter_presentation/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/notification_filter_presentation/NotificationFilterScreen.kt (Inbox), .../dashboard/NotificationDashboardScreen.kt and .../dashboard/widgets/*.kt, a prior mock-up /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/settings-nav-mockups.html and real screenshots in /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/captures/notifications/ (view the PNGs). Model: notification_filter_domain/.../model/NotificationItem.kt, NotificationPriority.kt, NotificationCategory.kt, and the delivery model in .../delivery/.

## Read first (the owner's own research)
Search for the owner's Glamorous Toolkit work and read it properly, not just the headings: /home/mini/Documents/repos/mstack/research/11-moldable-components.md, 12-paneweft-v1-in-code-views.md, 18-girba-wayne-oreilly.md, 20-gt4llm-and-liveness-tests.md; /home/mini/Documents/repos/mstack/README.md; /home/mini/Documents/repos/paneweft/README.md and docs/design.md; /home/mini/Documents/repos/phoe-nix/knowledge/research/agentic-practice-2026-11/11-moldable-components.md and 12-paneweft-v1-in-code-views.md; plus anything else `grep -ril "moldable\|glamorous\|gt4" /home/mini/Documents/repos/*/research /home/mini/Documents/repos/*/docs 2>/dev/null | head -40` turns up. Extract what Glamorous Toolkit's moldable development contributes as a language: objects with several custom views (inspector views), views chosen by the object's kind, small purpose-built views, live example-driven views, the 'every object can explain itself' idea, how views compose, and what the owner already concluded and tried (paneweft). Quote or paraphrase the owner's own conclusions and cite the file.

## Then survey, briefly and concretely (what each contributes to showing a notification, not a product tour)
Other UI libraries and notification-like idioms: Android (Material 3 Expressive, Compose canvas and Glance, Wear OS Tiles and complications, Android 16 progress-centric Live Updates, grouped and conversation notifications, notification channels and importance glyphs), iOS (Live Activities and Dynamic Island, notification summaries, Focus filters), Slack Block Kit and Microsoft Adaptive Cards (declarative payload to card), Observable Plot / Vega-Lite and Tufte-style small multiples and sparklines (marks and encodings), timeline and swimlane views (Gantt, git graph), email thread and triage tools (Superhuman, Hey 'Imbox', Gmail categories), Linear/Things/Todoist inbox triage, Bloomberg/terminal density, Apple Watch glanceables, Teenage Engineering style iconography, Material Symbols weights, status-light and signal conventions (traffic lights, TCAS, aviation annunciator panels with master caution). Add anything better you find. For each: the idea in one or two sentences, and what it would mean for a Farhan notification.

## Deliver
1. A vocabulary: the dimensions a notification has that text hides (priority, category, source app and its chattiness, arrival time versus its delivery moment, how long it has been waiting, budget cost, conversation or thread membership, whether it expects action, whether it repeats, its next delivery moment) and a proposed visual or spatial encoding for each (position, shape, colour, size, glyph, motion, grouping), with the constraints that matter on a phone (one-handed, glanceable, dark and light, colour-blind safety, no reliance on colour alone, text kept for content).
2. Four to six distinct display languages for the Inbox and the Overview, each named, with its rule in a sentence, what it makes easy, what it hides, and which of the owner's constraints it fits. Include at least: one moldable approach (a notification renders through a view chosen by its kind: message thread, payment, calendar, delivery, alert, one-time code, generic), one timeline or schedule-centred approach showing when each notification will arrive against the cadence and budget, one density or small-multiples approach, and one very quiet approach. State your top two recommendations for Farhan and the cost of building each in Compose (what to reuse from the existing widgets).
3. The HTML mock-up: three phone-width Inbox screens and two Overview widgets showing your top candidates side by side with the current text rows (use the Farhan dark palette from settings-nav-mockups.html; SVG for marks). Include a legend. No lorem ipsum: use plausible Farhan content (a chat app with 6 messages, a bank alert, a calendar reminder, a delivery update, a one-time code, a news app).
4. A short list of open questions for the owner.

Plain sentences, no eyebrow lines, cite files and URLs for every claim about the owner's research or a library. Time box about 60 minutes of wall clock; write early and keep both files current.

The three runs that finished:

- **Usage permission (`fix/usage-permission-package`, commit `653b60b`).** I confirmed the usage permission fix on the emulator. With the permission allowed, the old build showed "Usage permission is not granted" and the fixed build showed the real Usage page. The root-only grant in the grayscale code also uses the right package name now, but I could only compile that path, since the emulator isn't rooted.
- **Per-category Clear (`fix/clear-per-category`, commit `10dd0d1`).** Clear now removes only the selected priority's rows, on every page. It cancels deliveries and retained actions for those rows only. "Clear all" still clears everything, and the Cleared view's button is now "Delete cleared history". All 179 targeted tests pass; I haven't tried it on a device.
- **Snooze tests, first round.** The first set of failing tests is superseded by your timing rule. The Sol author is rewriting them for per-priority timing and the budget check at return.

An Opus reviewer is now going over the usage and clear branches; nothing goes to you until it reports back and I've pushed back on it at least once. The settings-menu builder is still reading the code, so I'm holding its check-in until it has something to look at.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.


Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

**Turn 1:** "use boat to build me both the ADB extraction APK and the latest Farhan APK with settings important export. then taildrop me them both." Done. APKs were built on Boat sandbox `bx_bngcafgz`, sent via `tailscale file cp … pixel-9a:`, and the sandbox was stopped.

**Turn 2:** the owner attached `Farhan settings rescue log 7f854af48d74.txt` (a Pixel crash: `ClassNotFoundException androidx.startup.InitializationProvider`). They asked me to examine Reverb (`/home/mini/Documents/repos/reverb`) and Shizuku to check the ADB connection process, to make sure it runs on an emulator and actually connects and extracts DB/files from an app, and to generalize it to any debuggable APK.

**Turn 3, messages in order:**
1. Usage page does not work no matter how often the permission is granted. Settings export was already done via the extractor, but they cannot find where to import. They want ALL settings unified into one menu reachable from the top menu, including appearance and theme. They want mock-ups for alternative dashboard navigation (icons not conflicting, not stacked in one corner).
2. Make snooze "fully fledged" for all apps, still marked pilot, not demo: "When I ask for a pilot, I expect it to be fully featured, even if experimental."
3. "No, you do the mock-up, sub-agents do the rest."
4. "Please switch to using a build loop in case that wasn't clear."
5. "Two small things, make sure that you use WorkQ to keep track of this all, and then I would also like for you to make it so that the clear button, in a particular category, only clears what is in that category, not everything overall."
6. "At the end of the queue, I would like to add the padding fix as a PR to upstream. In the meantime, we can keep working on the other details."
7. "bottom bar works for me, the rest of what you have there sounds great." Plus:
   - research alternative display languages for notifications beyond simple text: examine "my current research on glamorous toolkit, as well as other UI libraries";
   - snooze: "should not be a specific duration. It needs to be specific to what the budget allows and when the next notification moment is. How much flexibility does Android system have here? Are we able to access the notification details otherwise inside of Farhound and perhaps still activate it from within the app? If we can do this directly via APIs, then that's the preferred route. But if we must go through another means, then perhaps we must consider that."
8. "Please note that the next notification moment is specific to what category. Critical always go through directly, thus no snooze. High priority and medium priority have a specific cadence and then low priority has a cadence of a longer hour interval."
9. "Do the parallel research via subagent. Usage is not actually that low. Please do not stress about that."
10. A system-delivered task-completion batch (snooze red v1 [completed], usage-permission [completed], clear-category [completed]) arrived just before this summary request.

**Standing rules in force (global CLAUDE.md and harness):**
- "if you think this is a good idea, do it. Otherwise, suggest something else."
- Never open issues/forks/PRs/posts/upstream outreach without explicit approval. The owner approved the padding PR, but the draft must still be shown before `gh pr create` (build-loop §11).
- Skills live in mstack; omit eyebrow lines; copy goes through `writing-copy`.
- Show the journey (journey file + mock-ups as PNG/GIF in PR bodies).
- UI work inherits before it builds (brief names mock-up, original screen, prior pilots; build compared to mock-up in screenshot pairs before the owner sees it; `ui-brief-check`).
- Mock-ups are shown via T3 `html_preview` then `html_render`, HTML kept in the project's research dir, not claude.ai Artifacts.
- Taildrop to `pixel-9a` (personal profile), never `google-pixel-9a-work`.
- Pronouns: use they/them. Treat user email as private.
- Never push; commit only as the loop instructs.
- Subagents never use vigil orchestrator mode.
- One working Claude agent at a time; reviewers have a separate cap of one; Sol/Codex runs are not capped.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Platform and tooling:** Android app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Hilt), Nix dev shell, Boat sandbox (x86_64 Ubuntu VM). Headless emulator AVD `farhan-notification-pilot`, API 35 x86_64, KVM, `-gpu swiftshader_indirect`.
- **Nix socket repair after `boat resume`:**
  - `sudo systemctl stop nix-daemon.service nix-daemon.socket; sudo rm -f /nix/var/nix/daemon-socket/socket; sudo systemctl start nix-daemon.socket nix-daemon.service; sleep 3; sudo chmod 666 …/socket`
  - Detached jobs need `setpriv --ambient-caps -all --inh-caps -all`.
- **Wireless-debugging / ADB wire protocol:**
  - plain CNXN → adbd STLS → client STLS → TLS 1.3 handshake with client cert of the paired key → adbd sends its own CNXN (`adbd_wifi_secure_connect` = `handle_online` + `send_connect`) → OPEN/OKAY/WRTE/CLSE.
  - Never send a second CNXN after TLS (confirmed by Reverb `AdbStlsUpgrade` and Shizuku `AdbClient.kt`).
  - Pairing via libadb-android 3.1.1 (SPAKE2, Conscrypt `exportKeyingMaterial`).
- **libadb bug:** libadb-android 3.1.1 `AdbStream` never reports EOF when the peer closes while data is still queued (`mPendingClose=true`, `mIsClosed=false`). `run-as … id -u` hangs forever. Found by attaching `jdb` over JDWP (`adb forward tcp:N jdwp:PID`) to the debuggable helper.
- **Own wire client:** `AdbWireSession` reads frames on the calling thread with a 30 s socket timeout, replacing libadb for connect and exec; libadb is kept for pairing only.
- **Emulator adbd** logs "auth not required", so real-phone key acceptance is unverified.
- **Raw pull:**
  - `run-as <pkg> --user N tar -c -f - --exclude=./cache --exclude=./code_cache . 2>/dev/null`
  - validated by `TarIndex` (checksums, entries, end marker) and a 256 MiB bound
  - saved via SAF `CREATE_DOCUMENT`, verified by SHA-256 read-back.
- **Android notification model:**
  - NotificationListenerService with Farhan's delivery pipeline: `NotificationDeliveryCoordinator`, `DeliveryGate`, `NotificationDeliveryPolicy`, `PriorityDeliverySetting`, `DeliveryCadence` {IMMEDIATELY, EVERY_HOUR, EVERY_OTHER_HOUR, EVERY_THIRD_HOUR, ONCE_DAILY}.
  - Defaults: CRITICAL immediate/IGNORING budget; HIGH hourly; MEDIUM every other hour; LOW once daily (all RESPECTING).
  - Budget points per schedule period, hourly passthrough cap `MAX_HOURLY_PASSTHROUGH = 10`, `DeliveryTimeContext` boundaries (hourly; testing mode 3 min).
  - Native `snoozeNotification(key, ms)`: no public unsnooze; `getSnoozedNotifications()` rehydrates keys after restart; `REASON_SNOOZED = 18`.
  - Existing proxy path: cancel the source notification, later post a proxy and fire captured PendingIntents (`NotificationActionStore`).
- **Bug class:** Kotlin namespace `ly.com.tahaben.farhan` ≠ applicationId `ly.com.tahaben.farhan_alpha`, so AppOps rejects the package.
- **Build-loop process:**
  - orchestrator writes briefs, gates, mock-ups; Sol/Sonnet implement.
  - red tests → red gate verified by me → commit red → spec review (≤2 rounds) → green → review rounds (scored, ledger `review-ledger`, round 1 Sol/Opus never the author, round 2 Fable).
  - pilot rules: feature flag, bars agreed, targeted tests only, own branch.
  - UI briefs need an inheritance table plus fidelity pass by a different model before the owner sees screenshots.
  - 5-minute implementer check-in (read 1–5 files, ask 2–3 questions) recorded in the ledger.
  - Vigil session hold with a background `vigil keepalive --session --brief --orchestrator`.
- **WorkQ:** CLI `workq` (on/add/list/start/done/…); hook files owner requests as `workq add --from mN`.
- **T3 delegation:** `delegate_task` (providerInstanceId `codex` model `gpt-6.2-sol` options `{reasoningEffort:"high"}`; `claudeAgent` models `claude-sonnet-5-5`/`claude-opus-5-5` options `{effort:"high"}`). Steer via `t3_thread_send` to the child thread id (never the task id). A send to a finished child starts a fresh task. Codex mounts `.git` read-only, so the child commits via `git clone --shared` + bundle.
- **Environment limits:**
  - This host has 7 GB RAM, so no Gradle here (use Boat via `edge.research/bin/boat-run`, one build at a time under `flock /tmp/farhan-boat.lock`).
  - `html_preview` fails on this host (missing browser libs; `t3 browser setup` needs sudo and was not run), but `html_render` works.

## 3. Files and Code Sections

**Turn 2 helper work (all in `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan`, branch `pilot/settings-portability`, uncommitted):**
- `settings_rescue/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
  - Replaced the merge-style `androidx.startup.InitializationProvider` entry with `tools:node="remove"` (comment explains the crash). This fixes the Pixel crash.
- `settings_rescue/.../adb/AdbWire.kt` (new)
  - `AdbWireSession.connect(host, port, TlsUpgrade, …)` (CNXN→STLS→TLS→CNXN)
  - `open(destination): ExecStream` with `read()` returning -1 at CLSE
  - `close()` drains up to 1 MiB
  - `Frame` codec with magic/known-command/payload checks
  - `AdbWireException` {NotWirelessDebugging, PairingRequired(cause), ServiceRejected}
  - handshake/first-read IOExceptions other than `SocketTimeoutException` → `PairingRequired`.
- `adb/ConscryptTls.kt` (new)
  - `ConscryptTls(privateKey, cert): TlsUpgrade` using `SSLContext.getInstance("TLSv1.3", Conscrypt.newProvider())`, `SingleKeyManager`, accept-daemon trust manager.
- `adb/AdbShell.kt`
  - now takes `AdbWireSession`; added `archive(...)`, a `copyStream` helper; the libadb "Stream closed" workaround was removed.
- `adb/AdbCommand.kt`
  - added `Archive(target)` with destination `exec:run-as <pkg> --user N tar -c -f - --exclude=./cache --exclude=./code_cache . 2>/dev/null`.
- `adb/RemoteShell.kt`
  - added `archive(...)`.
- `adb/RescueAdbManager.kt`
  - doc note: used for pairing only.
- `bridge/AdbBridgeService.kt`
  - `withConnection` builds the key/cert from the identity and uses `AdbWireSession`; catch for `AdbWireException.PairingRequired`; new `BridgeRequest.Pull` handler.
- `bridge/BridgeProtocol.kt`
  - `OperationKind.PULL`, `BridgeRequest.Pull`, `BridgeEvent.Pulled(PullFacts)` and their wire encode/decode.
- `bridge/BridgeSupervision.kt`

1	# Argument, priorities, and behavior profiles
2	
3	Implementers begin immediately and have a work-grounded check-in roughly five
4	minutes into the batch. Every reviewer round needs one substantive exchange,
5	even an approval. Fable needs two; non-clean tier-one round four keeps two.
6	Challenge a material assumption, consequence or simpler option without inventing
7	disagreement.
8	
9	## Set the round focus
10	
11	Store a JSON object containing arrays of strings:
12	
13	```json
14	{
15	  "most_important": ["Revoking a share prevents subsequent content reads."],
16	  "invariants": ["Cached content must not bypass revocation."],
17	  "priority_concerns": ["security", "concurrency"],
18	  "lower_priority": ["Copy polish can wait."],
19	  "evidence": ["revoked_share_denies_read passed; device exercise unavailable."]
20	}
21	```
22	
23	The first, second and fifth arrays must be nonempty. State uncertainty honestly
24	when proof is missing. Priorities weight attention; they cannot waive a real
25	contract, security or data-loss defect. `context` updates later briefs; each
26	recorded round keeps its own snapshot. Set context before any new schema-2 round.
27	
28	```sh
29	review-ledger -l LED context --file focus.json
30	review-ledger -l LED brief --model EXACT_MODEL > review-brief.txt
31	```
32	
33	The brief includes focus and the compact behavior mask. Optional `--family sol`
34	explicitly permits a family aggregate if the exact model has no profile. An
35	unknown model never silently inherits observations about earlier weights.
36	
37	## Implementer check-in after work starts
38	
39	Start implementation without waiting for proposal approval. Note the start time.
40	Roughly five minutes into actual work, the orchestrator reads 1–5 relevant files,
41	including the current edits, then asks 2–3 concrete questions. Ask what remains
42	ambiguous and point to questionable assumptions or implementation choices in
43	those files. The implementer answers from the work; the orchestrator challenges
44	the answers where needed and settles direction before the questioned work
45	continues. This checks implementation bias rather than repeating planning.
46	
47	For example, after reading a handler and tests: What remains ambiguous? Why add
48	a second cancellation registry when the job already carries the state? Where
49	did the requirement to delete partial output come from? After the answers, the
50	orchestrator decides which state and behavior the implementation should use.
51	
52	Use an available session timer to make the check eligible around five minutes;
53	do not sleep or hold the implementer idle. The orchestrator can read files while
54	the implementer works and must use the supported messaging route for that live
55	agent. For a batch finishing sooner, perform the exchange at handoff. Raise known
56	blockers immediately rather than waiting for the check-in.
57	
58	Record implementer identity, batch/start time, the 1–5 inspected file paths,
59	2–3 actual questions and answers, orchestrator pushback, and the settled decision
60	with `review-ledger -l LED implementation-check --file checkin.json`.
61	The JSON fields are `agent`, timezone-qualified `started_at`, `inspected_files`,
62	`ambiguities`, `questions`, `pushback`, and `resolution`. Questions are 2–3 objects
63	with nonblank `question` and `answer` strings. Files are 1–5 distinct paths;
64	ambiguities is a string array, empty if none remain. Pushback and resolution are
65	nonblank strings. Explain why the current approach suffices if no correction is
66	needed. The ledger records elapsed time and rejects an exact duplicate. It accepts
67	a shorter batch's handoff exchange without making the agent wait. Recording
68	cannot establish that files were really read or that dialogue was substantive;
69	the orchestrator must do both.
70	
71	The earlier `plan`, `plan-answer`, and `plan-status` commands remain available
72	for optional explicit planning records and compatibility. Their READY status is
73	not a prerequisite to starting implementation. Reviewer argument gates are
74	unchanged.
75	
76	## Record review exchanges and findings
77	
78	Let the reviewer write its reply to a research output file through its harness.
79	The existing round parser saves findings, nit stash, hardening stash and stable
80	IDs. Do not create a second manually maintained concern list.
81	
82	```sh
83	review-ledger -l LED round --tier 1 --reviewer sol --author sonnet \
84	  --model EXACT_MODEL --effort VERIFIED_EFFORT --sha SHA --reply review.txt
85	review-ledger -l LED next
86	review-ledger -l LED brief --model EXACT_MODEL > argument-brief.txt
87	review-ledger -l LED argue --note exchange.txt
88	```
89	
90	`exchange.txt` contains both `Orchestrator:` and `Reviewer:` sections with their
91	actual exchange. For T3, every new review or recheck uses a new delegate with
92	prior context and objections. Native agents can use supported messaging. A
93	summary records the real speakers; it is not permission to fabricate dialogue.
94	The ledger rejects one-sided/empty notes and exact duplicates. It blocks a new
95	round or phase transition while an earlier exchange remains unfinished.
96	Revised reviewer SCORE/VERDICT lines update the round and preserve originals.
97	
98	Use `--requested-effort` to record a request separately from exposed `--effort`.
99	Record effective model and effort when exposed. Do not label a requested effort
100	as verified. Missing effort remains unknown. Observe priorities, finding classes,
101	review dispositions and source evidence when refreshing profiles.
102	
103	## Maintain small behavior masks
104	
105	`scripts/review-profile EXACT_MODEL` prints three strength and three weakness
106	slots, with evidence status. `--mask-only` prints the short adjustment sent to
107	agents. `--role implementation` selects the separate implementer observations.
108	
109	The data is `references/reviewer-profiles.json`. Nicknames describe behavior;
110	dated mappings associate exact versions and roles with them. Sparse slots remain
111	unknown. Family aggregates identify their supporting versions and require an
112	explicit fallback. A declined nit is not automatically wrong, and an accepted
113	nit is not independently proven correct. Never suppress an important finding
114	because of a profile.
115	
116	To refresh, extract original reviewer statements and dispositions from newly
117	recorded rounds, deduplicate copied replies, and cite source locators. Keep raw
118	history private in project research; commit only necessary observations and
119	pointers. Revise the mapping or mask when evidence changes. Do not rename the
120	archetype merely because a provider changes weights.

# Snooze pilot red report

Red v2 is based on `028541d` on `pilot/snooze`. The owner replaced the duration setting with per-priority cadence and a budget decision on return.

## Changes from red v1

- Removed `SnoozeDuration`, its tests, the snooze backup/restore tests, and the snooze integer case in `SettingsCatalogTest`. The rest of the catalog test is back at the pilot base.
- `SnoozeTimingTest` pins literal UTC target instants for all four batch cadences, exact-boundary arrival, local midnight, both Denver DST transitions, and three-minute testing mode. Every positive delay is checked for alignment and verified against `DeliveryClock.current` and `NotificationDeliveryPolicy.isBatchTickForCadence`. The actual batch poller's minimum wake-up delay is unsuitable for an exact native snooze near a tick. The timing stub returns zero.
- The policy tests keep the existing exclusions and add immediate-cadence HIGH and passthrough. CRITICAL uses a batch setting in its isolation test to prove that its exclusion does not depend on configured cadence. The new handler case exercises both CRITICAL and immediate HIGH at the native platform port.
- Replaced the v1 handler's unconditional consume expectations with allow-and-charge and deny-and-retry sequences. The tests cover exhausted points, hourly cap, zero points, no active period, duplicate callbacks inside a boundary, distinct keys retrying at the same boundary, settings changes before return, restart, Android removal, off behavior, and native call failure on an initial snooze. `RESNOOZED` is an event kind. The handler uses SDK constants for D6.
- The v1 tracker tests, twenty-event control, and no-legacy-source guard remain. The service and presentation still call `SNOOZE_DEMO`, `SNOOZE_MILLIS`, `SNOOZE_DEMO_PACKAGES`, and `maySnoozeInDemo` directly or transitively. The source guard stays red until green removes them. The empty exhaustive presentation branch now covers `RESNOOZED` as well as `FAILED`.

## Budget seam

`SnoozeReturnBudget.settleReturn(key, packageName, priority, at)` is suspendable and returns `Charged` or `RetryAt(instant)`. Green can map it to `NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.settleSnoozeReturn`, one operation under the shared `DeliveryGate.run`. Under the gate, resolve current settings and schedule, call `canDeliverNow`, and use `recordPassthrough` and the existing budget store and spend-entry path on success. The spend entry can identify the app and leave the title blank. Incoming return keys are transient inputs to accounting. The handler owns Android calls and tracker updates. A denied return must never debit points or the hourly counter.

The test fake uses the existing budget policy and passthrough charge calculation on an in-memory snapshot. It supplies literal retry deadlines as the port result, so the tests prove how the handler applies that result. The green coordinator needs its own verification for selecting the first funded cadence tick and persisting the charge through the existing budget path. The budget store currently has separate state-write and spend-append calls with coordinator recovery. Green needs to cover a partial write without charging twice and avoid marking any proxy row delivered. The chosen denial witnesses are 10:00 after the hourly cap and 12:00 after an exhausted, zero-point, or absent period at 09:00.

An Android snooze already scheduled keeps its absolute return time across schedule, cadence, budget, and zone changes. Returns are re-decided at that time. Burst returns spend in callback order, so the app-queue ranking is a pilot hardening item. If Android omits a cancellation callback, one future post of that stale key may be treated as a return. The spec calls for a daily retry bound without fixing a number. Red v2 pins the per-key boundary bound. The daily limit and its logging, plus behavior after a denied return whose native retry throws, remain green decisions.

## Targeted test failure summary

The first Boat run used the three targeted Gradle tasks with `--continue --no-daemon -q`. The domain suites had 27 expected assertion failures out of 179 tests per variant and the data suites had 15 out of 34 per variant. All 59 settings portability tests passed. The log is `/tmp/boat-run/snooze-20261120T120325Z-6f5e59.log`.

The data-only rerun includes the strengthened boundary test and the second-key witness. Its log is `/tmp/boat-run/snooze-20261120T120431Z-1412c9.log`. Both runs used the locked Boat checkout `/home/user/runs/snooze`. The XML reports show the following final counts.

| Module | Variant | Tests | Assertion failures | Errors | Skipped |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| notification_filter_domain | Debug | 179 | 27 | 0 | 0 |
| notification_filter_domain | Release | 179 | 27 | 0 | 0 |
| notification_filter_data | Debug | 35 | 16 | 0 | 0 |
| notification_filter_data | Release | 35 | 16 | 0 | 0 |
| settings_portability | JVM | 59 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

- Domain failed as expected on 15 policy cases (the stub returns a zero-delay snooze), 7 timing cases (the delay must be positive), 4 tracker cases (the stub retains no keys), and the source guard (legacy declarations and callers remain). The bounded event log passed.
- Data failed as expected on all 16 handler cases. The handler stub reports every post as unhandled and makes no native or budget calls. The denial fixtures reached their expected budget decisions before failing at the initial snooze witness.
- All 43 distinct Snooze contract failures were Truth assertions. All other tests in the targeted suites passed. Coordinator and service wiring, presentation compilation, and Android callback verification remain for green. No issue took over 30 minutes.

# Android notification snooze and in-app actions

## 1. Native snooze

**Duration and timing (SOURCE-READ, VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE).** The public API takes a positive `long` in milliseconds. AOSP rejects a null key, zero or negative timed durations, keys it cannot find, and users the listener cannot match. There is no explicit maximum duration in the inspected path. Adding an extreme value to the current wall clock can overflow. AOSP caps concurrent snoozes at 500 across the helper, including notification groups and persisted entries. The call returns void and queues the operation. Success requires confirmation through a removal callback or a fresh snapshot. The API 35 probe observed zero as a no-op and accepted both 1 ms and 24 h. It verified the 24 h deadline in the alarm dump without waiting a day. [NLS15], [NMS15] `snoozeNotificationInt`, `SnoozeNotificationRunnable`, [SH15] `CONCURRENT_SNOOZE_LIMIT`, `canSnooze`, `scheduleRepost`.

**Exact alarm and Doze (SOURCE-READ, VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE).** The system schedules an `RTC_WAKEUP` alarm with `setExactAndAllowWhileIdle` under system identity. AOSP's alarm service exempts core callers from the ordinary minimum lead time and sets the unrestricted idle flag for this system alarm. The usual per-app idle quota is therefore a poor model for snooze. Callback time still includes alarm dispatch, notification enqueue, ranking and listener processing. Existing deadlines are wall-clock timestamps. A timezone change does not recalculate them for the new local cadence. A wall-clock correction can change the elapsed wait. This path does not require Farhan to hold exact-alarm access. [SH15] `scheduleRepostAtTime`, [AMS15] `set`, `setImplLocked`, `adjustDeliveryTimeBasedOnDeviceIdle`, [AlarmManager].

**Process death and reboot (SOURCE-READ, VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE for listener death).** Snoozed records live in the notification manager in the system process. Killing the listener and letting Android reconnect left the records, timers and usable source tokens in place. The policy XML persists keys and future timestamps or context IDs. It does not serialize the original notification or its tokens. At boot the system reschedules future timers, but a timer with no in-memory record has nothing to repost. If the source app posts the same key before the saved deadline, Android can put that new record back under snooze until the deadline. A notification that the source never reposts can be lost across reboot. [SH15] `getSnoozed`, `writeXml`, `readXml`, `scheduleRepostsForPersistedNotifications`, `repost`, [NMS15] `onBootPhase`, `EnqueueNotificationRunnable.enqueueNotification`.

**Callbacks, identity and alerts (SOURCE-READ, VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE).** A posted notification leaves with `onNotificationRemoved(..., REASON_SNOOZED)` (18). Timed return enqueues a fresh record with the source package, ID and tag. The probe received `onNotificationPosted` with the same key and a new `StatusBarNotification.postTime`. The publisher's `Notification.when` stayed the same. Group and ranking metadata can be recomputed, so the unchanged key observed for a standalone notification is not an identity guarantee for every group summary. [NLS], [SBN15] `key`, `getPostTime`, [NMS15] `onStart` (snooze callback), `enqueueNotificationInternal`, `snoozeNotificationLocked`.

- Timer expiration calls `repost(..., false)`. The privileged system-listener early-release path can pass `muteOnReturn=true` and set the new record's `postSilently`. The regular timed API exposes no mute option. `FLAG_ONLY_ALERT_ONCE` applies to an update in the attention helper. In the probe an original with that flag returned with a system beep event. Whether it sounds, vibrates or shows heads-up depends on channel importance, device and user settings, grouping, Do Not Disturb and alert throttling. The heads-up path also makes its own decision, including an age test on the publisher's `when`. [SH15] `mBroadcastReceiver`, [NMS15] `unsnoozeNotificationFromSystemListener`, `enqueueNotificationInternal`, [NAH15] `shouldMuteNotificationLocked`, `buzzBeepBlinkLocked`, [HUN15] `shouldHeadsUpWhenAwake`.
- The listener can snooze again in its return callback. The active post and attention decision come first. A probe that called snooze synchronously in the callback received the removal callback 8 ms later and the Android event log still recorded a beep for the return. The 8 ms is a callback interval, with system enqueue and UI work outside that measurement. Farhan's classification and budget path can add latency. I did not measure a heads-up or shade flash. There is no listener guarantee of hiding a denied return before the owner can notice it. [NMS15] `PostNotificationRunnable`, `snoozeNotificationInt`, [NAH15] `buzzBeepBlinkLocked`.

**Eligibility (SOURCE-READ, VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE for ongoing).** The inspected listener snooze path has no blanket rejection for `FLAG_ONGOING_EVENT`, foreground-service flags, `FLAG_NO_CLEAR`, the listener's own package, or call and alarm categories. The API 35 listener snoozed an ongoing notification. System UI dismissal rules and listener cancellation rules are separate. App-defined summaries can snooze their children, and snoozing an only child can also snooze its summary. An auto-group summary matching the AOSP auto-group rule can be removed without being retained for independent return. A new group child can bring back a snoozed summary. Keep the pilot's exclusions as Farhan policy. Skipping summaries as direct inputs alone does not prevent collateral group changes. Privileged and promoted notifications, foreground services, calls and alarms were not exercised. [NMS15] `snoozeNotificationInt`, `SnoozeNotificationRunnable.snoozeLocked`, `isSnoozable`, `EnqueueNotificationRunnable.enqueueNotification`, `cancelNotificationFromListenerLocked`, [Android 14].

## 2. Early release

The regular listener has **no public unsnooze operation through API 37**. It does have an effective early-release route on API 35. Fetch the hidden key, then replace its timer with a short positive duration. Keep that behavior experimental until it passes on supported devices. [NLS], [SDK17], [NMS15] `snoozeNotificationInt`, `findInCurrentAndSnoozedNotificationByKeyLocked`, [SH15] `scheduleRepostAtTime`.

| Route | Evidence | What it gives up |
| --- | --- | --- |

[NLS15] `getSnoozedNotifications`, [NMS15] `getSnoozedNotificationsFromListener`. | Read-only. A record can still be listed after source cancellation. |
| Call `snoozeNotification(key, shortDuration)` again | VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE. A normal listener, separate from the publisher, replaced a 24 h timer with 1 ms and got the original back in 220 ms from command receipt. The API 35 service searches both active and hidden records and replaces the alarm. The same implementation accepts a positive duration computed from a desired future instant. [NMS15] `findInCurrentAndSnoozedNotificationByKeyLocked`, [SH15] `snooze`, `scheduleRepostAtTime`. | Timer replacement on a hidden key is implementation behavior. Changing the Android setting has broad effects and depends on the system build. |

## 3. Reading active and snoozed details

**Both query paths request full records (SOURCE-READ, VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE for the probe payload).** After `onListenerConnected`, `getActiveNotifications()` and `getSnoozedNotifications()` request `TRIM_FULL`. Both use the same server-side profile, package/type and sensitive-content filtering. Each returns a list of `StatusBarNotification` objects the service can access. The snoozed query can return null on a remote error. Notification data comes from the source app and may be missing. Some media or custom content can also require separately granted access to a URI. The callback for removal can be a light copy. Read details from the posted or queried record. [NLS15] `getSnoozedNotifications`, `getActiveNotifications`, `cleanUpNotificationList`, `onNotificationRemoved`, [NMS15] `addToListIfNeeded`, `isVisibleToListener`, `updateUriPermissions`.

| Field | What Farhan can read | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who posted it | Package, operation package, user, ID, tag, key, group key, group/sort information and flags. `Notification.category` describes what the app says it is. | SOURCE-READ. [SBN15] `getPackageName`, `getOpPkg`, `getUser`, `getId`, `getTag`, `getKey`, `getGroupKey`; [Notification]. |
| Text and messaging | `extras` can include `EXTRA_TITLE`, `EXTRA_TEXT`, `EXTRA_BIG_TEXT`, lines, subtext and summary. `MessagingStyle` exposes messages, including text, person, timestamps and optional attachment URI, when supplied. Custom views supply no reliable semantic text schema. | SOURCE-READ, with basic text and big text VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE. [Notification], [MessagingStyle], [Message]. |
| Icons and progress | Small/large icons, picture or other image extras where supplied, and progress, max and indeterminate extras. `ProgressStyle` on API 36 adds tracker-specific data. An icon handle does not guarantee a cross-package load, for example when its URI is inaccessible. | SOURCE-READ for Android 15 fields, icon presence VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE. DOC-ONLY for `ProgressStyle`. [N15] `getSmallIcon`, `getLargeIcon`, `EXTRA_PROGRESS`, `visitUris`; [ProgressStyle]. |

Active ranking can add assistant-suggested replies and actions. A snoozed record has no entry in the active `RankingMap`. SystemUI's suggested actions and app-supplied actions can differ. | SOURCE-READ for ranking. Content, delete and reply tokens in both queries VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE. [N15] `Action`, `contentIntent`, `deleteIntent`; [NLS15] `Ranking`, [NMS15] `makeRankingUpdateLocked`. |
| Channel and dates | `Notification.getChannelId()` works on the record. Active ranking can provide the channel object and importance. Companion/assistant checks protect separate channel enumeration. `postTime` is the system post timestamp, `when` is app supplied and `EXTRA_SHOW_WHEN` controls its presentation. Neither date is the snooze deadline. | SOURCE-READ. Both timestamps VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE. [SBN15] `getPostTime`, [N15] `getChannelId`, `when`, `EXTRA_SHOW_WHEN`; [NMS15] `verifyPrivilegedListener`, `makeRankingUpdateLocked`. |

A listener restart can reconstruct the snoozed list and reacquire the publisher's live tokens while the system still holds them. This is different from persisting your own token store after interception. The probe recovered title, text, big text, icon, open, delete and reply after reconnection, then sent open and reply to the separate source package. These queries do not identify which app initiated the snooze. [SH15] `getSnoozed`, [NMS15] `getSnoozedNotificationsFromListener`, [PendingIntent]. ## 4. Open, actions and cancellation

**Sending the token (VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE, SOURCE-READ).** A live source token is an Android capability. `PendingIntent.send` runs the publisher's specified operation using the token's creator identity. The probe sent a content broadcast after snoozing and after listener cancellation, and the source received both. It also sent a snoozed reply after listener restart. For replies, populate the original result keys with `RemoteInput.addResultsToIntent` and send the resulting intent through the action token. The token must accept fill-in data, so an immutable token cannot carry a filled-in reply. Follow the action's authentication requirement and show authenticated actions only after unlock. An activity token is subject to the sender and creator background-activity-start rules. Use an explicit foreground user tap and test activity, broadcast and reply actions separately. Successful dispatch alone proves neither an activity launch nor that the source performed the intended business action. [PendingIntent], [PIR15] `sendInner`, [RemoteInput], [Notification.Action], [Activity security].

- **Snooze tests (`pilot/snooze`, commit `938827f`).** I re-ran them on Boat. Of the new snooze tests, 27 fail on the domain side and 16 on the data side, the same counts Sol reported. That check either charges it and leaves it, or snoozes it again to the next moment that can deliver.
- **Cross-model spec review.** It waits for the reviewer slot, which the Opus review of the usage and clear branches is using. When that finishes, a different model reviews the spec and tests before any implementation starts.

  - Farhan can fire the original app's own tap and reply actions from inside the app.
  - There is no public "unsnooze". The workaround is to snooze again for a very short time.

  The recommendation section isn't in yet, so I'll summarise it once it lands.
- **Settings-hub build.** Its reply to my three questions hasn't arrived.

## 5. Recommendation

Keep **B as the default when budget and ordering must be enforced**. Pilot **C** for the owner who values source identity and wants to read or act while a notification is held. For C's **Deliver now**, try native timer replacement first on supported devices. Treat the gesture as the explicit decision to advance that item, with the existing budget ledger recording whichever override policy the owner chooses. Keep Open and Reply separate from delivery. Avoid a proxy fallback while a native record might still return.

| Approach | What it fits | What decides against it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. Native snooze, then budget at return | Preserves the publisher, channel and action tokens. Android handles the timer through listener death and can wake from Doze. Critical and immediate items can pass straight through. | Android can alert before Farhan decides. Returns arriving together spend in callback order unless the design changes. Reboot can lose payloads. Same-key updates, group operations and failed snooze requests complicate accounting. |
| B. Current cancel-and-proxy path | Farhan can select and order the queue before posting a batch and charge only the chosen items. The queue controls cadence changes and explicit early delivery. Initial interception still follows the original post. | The early cancellation can fire the publisher's delete token. A proxy belongs to Farhan. The bounded in-memory `NotificationActionStore` can expire or lose tokens, and cancellation leaves no native record to recover after restart. |
| C. Native snooze plus a live in-app list | Preserves the advantages of A and lets the owner read and act before a return. Requery on connect, screen entry and action, with callbacks to invalidate known rows. Offer Open and compatible actions from the live record. | Inherits A's alert, reboot and budget risks. The list can contain canceled items with no removal event. It can include snoozes created by the user or another listener. A proxy-only Deliver now can duplicate the original because public per-key cancellation skips hidden records. A short native re-snooze avoids that deliberate duplicate where it works. |

This needs a change to the current spec before C ships. D8 and I3 prohibit keeping or showing content and keys. An opt-in inbox that reads the live, redacted records and never persists payloads is a separate decision. Track ownership if Farhan must limit the list or budget to its own snoozes. Rehydrating from every snoozed key alone cannot establish that ownership or recognize a return that occurred while Farhan was disconnected.

For A and C, keep initial eligibility conservative, including groups whose other children or summary could be affected. Base next-moment calculation on the existing cadence and schedule. Calculate a positive delay and handle late callbacks, no-op requests, and process gaps explicitly. B is the only evaluated approach that applies Farhan's budget before Android posts its batch. A fast return callback cannot give A or C that property. The decisive experiment was an Android alert followed by an immediate re-snooze. The sound had already been requested before Farhan could deny it.

Farhan comparison is based on `NotificationService.kt` (`processNotificationPosted`, `postProxyNotification`, `CapturedAction`), `NotificationActionStore.kt`, `research/notification-pilot-contract.md`, `research/notification-restoration-feasibility.md` and the v2 block of `research/snooze-pilot-spec.md`.

The probe used two standalone APKs, a source package and a normal listener package, with a high-importance channel and synthetic data. The initial attempt overlapped with the already installed Farhan build, which canceled the fixture's active records and later posted fixture proxies. I paused Farhan's listener grant for the valid trials, without reinstalling Farhan or clearing its data. I temporarily enabled deep idle for one trial because both idle modes started disabled. I restored Farhan's grant and the original idle configuration, removed both probe APKs and confirmed the fixture's snoozed list was empty. Four synthetic Farhan proxies from the initial attempt remained in the shade. The emulator was left running.

Timing uses monotonic milliseconds from the listener's receipt of its test command to its posted callback. The persisted wall-clock deadline and new notification `postTime` help separate alarm/enqueue timing from listener delivery. These are single trials, not latency bounds.

| Restart and action tokens | Listener PID 2241 died. PID 2474 reconnected and listed three hidden records with text and every fixture token. A content broadcast and a filled-in reply reached the source process. | VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE. [NMS15] `getSnoozedNotificationsFromListener`; probe log. |
| Alert and callback re-snooze, IDs 21 and 22 | System beep event on both returns, including ID 21 with `ONLY_ALERT_ONCE`. The `notification_alert` event supplied the audible signal. The emulator ran headless. I did not record physical sound. | VERIFIED-ON-DEVICE for the system event and callbacks. ## Reproduce

The [API 35 transcript](snooze-android-probe/api35.txt) contains the synthetic listener events and Android alert events used for the device claims.

[Probe.java](snooze-android-probe/Probe.java) contains the listener and source receiver. [install.sh](snooze-android-probe/install.sh) builds them with the Boat SDK, signs with a disposable local key and grants the fixture's access on the emulator. [control.sh](snooze-android-probe/control.sh) sends test commands, restarts the listener and reads logs. The fixture runs on a disposable test emulator only. The scripts build standalone APKs without Gradle.

After the source notification first appears in `control.sh log`, issue a snooze request. To reproduce the 20 s observation and the 24 h replacement, run the following on Boat. Check the log between posting and snoozing because Android delivers posts asynchronously.

```bash
bash install.sh
bash control.sh source --ei id 21 --ez once true
bash control.sh log
bash control.sh listener --es op snooze --ei id 21 --el ms 20000
bash control.sh shell cmd notification snoozed
bash control.sh source --ei id 25 --ez ongoing true
bash control.sh log
bash control.sh listener --es op snooze --ei id 25 --el ms 86400000
bash control.sh shell dumpsys alarm
bash control.sh restart
bash control.sh log
bash control.sh listener --es op open --ei id 25
bash control.sh listener --es op reply --ei id 25
bash control.sh listener --es op cancel --ei id 25
bash control.sh listener --es op snooze --ei id 25 --el ms 1
bash control.sh shell dumpsys notification --noredact
bash control.sh shell logcat -d -b events -s notification_alert
```

Use ID 301 with duration 300000 for the five-minute trial. For callback re-snooze, post ID 22, arm that ID with `--es op arm`, then snooze it for 3500 ms. For source cancellation, post ID 23, snooze it for 20000 ms, then run `bash control.sh source --ei id 23 --es op cancel` and read before and after expiry. Read the notification alert event as key, buzz, beep, blink and politeness state. [NAH15] `buzzBeepBlinkLocked`.

For the forced-Doze trial I posted ID 28, ran `dumpsys deviceidle enable deep` and `dumpsys deviceidle force-idle deep`, snoozed it for 12000 ms, and checked its callback with the emulator still in `IDLE`. I restored the prior state with `dumpsys deviceidle unforce` and `dumpsys deviceidle disable deep`.

content.text:
The Android research landed. It answers your questions, and it exposes a problem with the snooze design you chose.

**Can Farhan read a snoozed notification and act on it from inside the app?** Yes, tested on the emulator. After Farhan's listener was killed and restarted, it still read the full title, text and icon of three snoozed notifications. It then fired the original app's tap action and a typed reply, and both reached that app. So a "Snoozed" list inside Farhan is feasible through public APIs, with no proxy copies. To "deliver now", Farhan snoozes the item again for 1 ms and the original comes back in about 0.2 s. That is a workaround, not a documented unsnooze, which doesn't exist.

**How flexible is the timing?** Android snoozes to an exact moment, even in deep Doze (12 s snooze, back after 12.2 s). It survives Farhan being killed. There is a cap of 500 snoozes at once.

**Two problems with budget-at-return snooze (your design):**
1. Android posts the notification back, possibly with a sound, before Farhan can decide. If the budget says no and Farhan snoozes it again, one beep has already happened. The emulator logged a beep on both returns. I've put this in the spec and the settings text; it won't be hidden.
2. After a reboot, Android keeps only the key and the deadline, not the notification itself. It comes back only if the source app posts it again. This is read from the source and not tested. It hurts most for Low, which is once a day.

Because of the first problem, the researcher recommends keeping the current cancel-and-proxy path where the budget must be strict, and treating native snooze as a pilot beside it. That is what the pilot is. I've kept your design and added these limits to the spec, so it's a fair comparison.

**Decisions for you:**
- Should I add the in-app "Snoozed" list (read, Open, Reply, Deliver now) as a second slice after the snooze pilot? It needs a spec change, because the spec currently forbids keeping or showing notification text. I'd say yes, and read the text live without saving it.
- Is it fine to ship the pilot with the one-beep-on-denial and reboot-loss limits written into the settings text? I think so, since it's a pilot.

Next, a different model reviews the spec and tests once the reviewer slot frees up. Sol hasn't started the green work yet.

What works:
- **Shared rule:** listing, ID selection and deletion are all built from one SQL predicate (`INBOX_PREDICATE`), at the cutoff of the query on screen.
- **Atomic and limit-safe:** the select and delete run in one Room transaction, inside the coordinator's gate with `NonCancellable`. Nothing binds an ID list, so SQLite's variable limit can't be hit.
- **Same set:** the IDs deleted are exactly the IDs whose delivery events are invalidated.

- **All:** unchanged.

1. **[should]** `notification_filter_presentation/.../NotificationFilterState.kt:25`, `showCleared -> Cleared(priorityFilter)`

Orchestrator: thanks, good review. Three places I want to push back before I accept it. Answer briefly, from code, edit nothing.

1. Finding 5 (skip `invalidateDeleted` and proxy cancels for Cleared). You say cleared rows have no proxies. Prove it from the code: can a row become `cleared` while its proxy is still posted or a delivery event is still in flight (mark-as-cleared from the inbox, a failed open, a source cancel)? If any path leaves an event or proxy alive for a cleared id, skipping invalidation reopens the stale-callback hole you praised in "what works". Also, are `NotificationManager.cancel` calls for a nonexistent id really binder calls we should avoid, or is the real cost the per-id loop inside the gate? Would batching the ids (one gate hold, no per-id suspension) be enough, and cheaper to get right than special-casing Cleared?
2. Finding 6 (high-water mark). The old All clear had the same behaviour and nobody called it a bug. A user who presses "Clear Low" accepts that rows arriving in the next milliseconds go too, and a row that arrives after the press but before the gate frees is the same case as one arriving a moment later. Why is this worth new state and a new predicate term, rather than a documented limit? I lean to decline it. Convince me or agree.
3. Finding 4 (empty-state flash): did the base (717faf6) already clear the lists on a chip tap, or is that new in this branch? Quote the base lines. If it pre-existed, it is out of scope for this fix and I will log it, not change it.

I accept findings 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and the B items as should-fix.
