Agreed, and I've started a planning run. It has no effect on the combined APK's timeline.

**What the run will do:**
- **Inventory:** it will list what tests exist today in three groups: tests that run on the computer alone, tests that need the emulator, and the emulator scripts. Boat timings will show where the time goes.
- **Classification:** for each emulator-dependent test, and for the evidence runs planned for snooze, sound control, the apps list and the layout-shift probe, it says which of three groups the test belongs to.
  - **Plain code:** logic tested with fake stand-ins for Android.
  - **Android simulated on the computer:** a tool called Robolectric. This covers database migrations, screen tests with screenshot comparison, and basic notification calls. It will name exactly what Robolectric does not simulate, such as snooze timing and Do Not Disturb rule behaviour.
  - **Real device only:** how Android really handles snooze returns, DND rules, alerts, calls and group cancels, plus performance.
- **Harness proposal:** a shared set of fakes, and a way to stop them drifting from real Android. One test suite runs against both the fake and the emulator occasionally. It also covers what production code needs to be a replaceable piece to be testable, how the checks split by speed, and a measured estimate of time saved.
- **First slice:**
  - **Migration test:** the Room migration test moves to Robolectric if it works there.
  - **Screenshot tests:** one each for the apps list and the inbox filter chips.
  - **Snooze contract tests:** a test layer around the snooze platform piece.

The snooze work keeps running on the emulator as planned. If the migration test moves off the emulator later, that only saves time on future runs.

I also fixed a labelling slip on my side. The snooze item was counted as a Claude run when it's Sol, and that blocked this new run for a moment. It's corrected now and nothing was lost.

But the spec as written would make the phone worse than today in three ways the owner would not notice:

- **Calls:** mirroring the owner's call settings narrows calls.
- **Owner's own DND:** the bypass channel lets Farhan alerts through the owner's own Do Not Disturb modes.
- **Exceptions:** notifications Farhan lets through today go silent.

Claims I make from my memory of AOSP source, not from reading it in this round, are marked **(recall, needs device test)**.

## MUST

**M1. S4 call mirroring narrows calls; it does not mirror them.** (S4, invariant 4, mock-up "Calls" card)
- What an ordinary target-35 app can read:
  - `getNotificationPolicy()` returns either the app's implicit-rule policy or, before one exists, the manual "Do Not Disturb" mode's stored policy. Research line 154 says this.
  - On the emulator that stored policy is `priorityCallSenders=PRIORITY_SENDERS_STARRED` (`dnd/api35-recovery.txt:26`, `calls/api35-calls.txt:11`). That is a setting that only applies while the owner's DND is on.
  - `getConsolidatedNotificationPolicy()` is the merge of whatever is active, Farhan's own rule included, so the owner's part can't be separated out.
  - `getAutomaticZenRules()` returns only Farhan's own rules.
  - Android 15+ has many modes (Bedtime, Driving, DND, custom), each with its own call policy. "The owner's call settings" is not one thing an app can read.
- Copying the readable policy into Farhan's rule gives starred-only calls whenever the owner's DND is off. Today all calls ring then. Transcript rows 7–10 (`calls/api35-calls.txt`, research lines 251–252) show exactly that failure: first call gets no ring and no vibration.
- Invariant 4 claims the transcripts verify mirroring. They verify the opposite: only rows 5/6 and 11/12 match baseline, and those used calls from **anyone**.
- **Fix:** drop mirroring. Farhan's rule always allows calls from anyone and repeat callers. Under strictest-wins this is the identity element for the call fields:
  - DND off: only Farhan's rule is active, so all calls pass (rows 5/6 = 1/2).
  - Owner's mode on: their stricter call policy wins.
- This removes the "re-read when they change" machinery entirely.
- Strictest-wins **for calls** with a second rule was never tested: the research line 152 two-rule trial used proxy notifications, not calls. The S4 disclaimer says calls with a second rule were "tested on one emulator only"; they were not tested at all. **Needs device test** (owner's DND with starred calls + Farhan rule + an injected non-starred call).

**M2. The bypass channel widens the owner's own DND.** (Intent "never touches the owner's own DND"; States "the consolidated policy still blocks the alert")
- The AOSP default DND policy has `allowPriorityChannels=true` (`dnd/api35-recovery.txt:26`).
- Research line 152 shows a second mode blocks the proxy only when that mode **denies** priority channels.
- So while sound control is on, Farhan's elected alerts break through the owner's Bedtime or DND, where the original app's notification would have been blocked. Farhan's channel will likely also appear under every mode's "Apps that can interrupt" **(needs device test, Pixel Modes UI)**.
- **Fix (owner decision; my default):** when the consolidated filter or policy is detectably stricter than Farhan's rule, post the elected item on the normal proxy channel so the owner's mode decides.
- Disclose the residual case: an owner mode whose policy is looser than Farhan's on every field is masked and can't be detected (research line 177).
- Correct the States sentence.

**M3. Notifications Farhan passes through today go silent.** (S2; `NotificationService.kt:304`, `NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:175`)
- `passThrough = systemExempt || exceptions || CRITICAL` leaves the original untouched with no proxy.
- Today those items sound natively. Under the rule they are intercepted. That includes the owner's exception apps, CRITICAL items, and `CATEGORY_MISSED_CALL` / `SYSTEM` / `SERVICE`.
- S4's "screener is CRITICAL in Farhan and untouched" means it goes silent unless its channel bypasses DND or Android treats it as a call. Research line 258: "The screener's own channel determines its silence."
- S2 defines "elected" as "what the existing pipeline already decides to deliver", but pass-through items are never "delivered".
- **Fix:** pass-through items while the rule is held either get an alerting breakthrough duplicate (with a stated duplicate and cancel lifecycle) or are named in the enable disclaimer. My default is the duplicate for CRITICAL and exception apps.

**M4. Messaging updates never sound.** (S2; `NotificationService.kt:129`; `NotificationFilterDataModule.kt:62-64`; coordinator lines 176–181)
- A source update to an already-delivered key goes through `refresh` → `silent = true`, plus `setOnlyAlertOnce(true)` on the same tag.
- Today the second Messenger message still beeps natively before Farhan cancels the original. Under the rule, only the first message of a conversation ever sounds.
- Messenger is the mock-up's own example.
- **Fix:** define update semantics for elected items. New content (new post time, source not only-alert-once) re-alerts on the breakthrough channel, subject to dedupe and rate limit.

**M5. Farhan keeps muting when it can no longer elect anything.** (S5, S7)
- `onNotificationPosted` returns early when `isNotificationServiceStatsEnabled()` is false (`NotificationService.kt:240`; also :287). The same happens on intake overflow (:256) and when the app main switch is off.
- In every one of these the rule stays active and nothing breaks through: everything goes silent with no alerts.
- **Fix:** the hold has preconditions:
  - all three grants are present;
  - the breakthrough channel still bypasses DND at a non-zero importance;
  - the filter is enabled;
  - the listener connected within N minutes.
- Any failed precondition makes the reconciler release the rule, enter a Suspended state, and say why. Use an exact alarm (`SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` is already in `notification_filter_data/.../AndroidManifest.xml:5`) as a dead-man check for listener liveness.
- Distinguish **Suspended** (Farhan released it and may resume once the preconditions hold) from **Paused** (the owner stopped it; needs a fresh tap).

**M6. A rule can be left with the flag off.** (Invariant 2 vs States "reinstall")
- Paths that reach it: Clear storage while held; the `notification_experiment_*` flag being imported off; restore from backup; downgrade.
- In each case the flag reads off but Android still holds an active Farhan rule.
- "With the flag off … no rule exists" therefore requires the reconciler to run **regardless of the flag**: if no persisted desired-On state exists, remove any owned rule found by conditionId.
- Downgrading to a build without this code cannot clean up. Make "Turn Off before installing another build" a disclaimer, and name the `farhan_alpha` versus main package case: two builds means two rules.

**M7. Rule identity: use conditionId, not name.** (States "find by name and owner package")
- `getAutomaticZenRules()` already returns only the caller's rules.
- On Android 15+ the user can likely rename a mode **(recall, needs device test)**. The probe's second rule had the same owner package (research line 152), so package alone does not identify the rule either.
- Adopt by stored id, else by a Farhan-fixed `conditionId`.
- On uninstall AOSP likely deletes the package's rules, and Android 15 may restore user customisations when the same pkg+conditionId is re-added **(recall, needs device test)**. So "reinstall" is really clear-data or backup-restore.

**M8. Persistence order as written is impossible.**
- Research line 179 says to persist desired state "in the same transaction as the owned rule ID", but the id only exists after `addAutomaticZenRule` returns.
- Spec the crash windows:
  1. persist `{desired: On, generation, phase: Creating}` with `commit()`;
  2. add the rule;
  3. persist the id;
  4. activate;
  5. persist Held.
- A crash anywhere in that sequence must be adopted or removed by conditionId on the next reconcile.
- The existing flag pattern uses `apply()` (`DefaultPreferences.kt:311`). Sound-control state needs a synchronous `commit()` in its own store.

**M9. Import and backup can turn the mute on silently.** (S10)
- If the enable bit follows the `Experiments` pattern (S8 says "under the same flag"), it matches the `notification_experiment_` → `Configuration` prefix (`SettingsCatalog.kt:104`). Export, import and rescue conversion would then carry "On" to another phone, skipping the grants and disclaimers.
- `allowBackup="true"` with empty rules (`app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:28-31`, `backup_rules.xml`) also restores the id and desired-On state.
- **Fix:**
  - enable bit → `ImportReset(Bool(false))`;
  - rule id, generation and phase → `Excluded(INTERNAL)`;
  - exclude the sound-control prefs file from cloud backup and device transfer;
  - election lists stay `Configuration`.

**M10. The ZenPolicy must be fully specified.** (S1)
- Unset ZenPolicy fields inherit the user's default policy **(recall, needs device test)**.
- Every field must be set explicitly:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Calls | anyone |
| Repeat callers | allowed |
| Alarms | allowed |
| Media | allowed by default (otherwise videos and music go quiet) |
| System | owner decides; touch and lock sounds otherwise mute |
| Priority channels | allowed |
| Messages, conversations, reminders, events | disallowed |
| Visual effects | all shown (otherwise notifications vanish from heads-up and the shade) |
| Device effects | null |

- S1 says "everything else off", which leaves visual effects undefined. The call probe used `showAllVisualEffects()` and `allowReminders(true)` (`calls/Probe.java:100-103`).

**M11. The breakthrough channel has a creation-order trap.** (S2)
- `setBypassDnd` is honoured only when the channel is **created** while the app has policy access **(recall, needs device test)**.
- A channel deleted and recreated with the same id gets its old settings back.
- So the channel is created only after the policy-access grant. Recovery after a lost bypass uses a new versioned id, never delete-and-recreate.
- The existing `PROXY_CHANNEL_ID` is created unconditionally at :217, so the new channel must not follow that pattern.

## SHOULD

- **S1. Two contradictions about owner edits.**
  - Spec S5: "If the owner stops or edits Farhan's rule in Settings, latch Paused." Research line 228: "If the owner invokes or edits a mode while held, allow it to be the active owner mode for a bounded window, then reapply the owned rule."
  - The research also contradicts itself (line 177 says latch Paused).
  - My default: a **stop** latches Paused. An **edit** is adopted, shown, and never overwritten.
  - Detecting an edit by comparing the read-back policy can fire falsely if Android normalises fields. **Needs device test.**
- **S2. The rule-status broadcast is missing.** Add `ACTION_AUTOMATIC_ZEN_RULE_STATUS_CHANGED` and API 35's `getAutomaticZenRuleState()` to the reconciler inputs (research line 177 lists them; spec S5 omits them).
  - Specify the `Condition` source for each call: `SOURCE_USER_ACTION` only from the enable or resume tap.
  - An off-then-on toggle clears the user's override **(recall, needs device test)**, and that is exactly what S8's window does.
- **S3. Missing state: owner activates Farhan's rule while Farhan wants it off.** This happens if manual invocation is allowed (research line 179 recommends it). Pin a decision.
- **S4. Rule deleted or revoked.**
  - Desired On with the rule missing → Paused, never recreated.
  - Settings likely removes the app's rules when DND access is revoked, but a listener-implied policy grant (research line 27) can vanish without removing the rule **(needs device test)**.
  - The status notification must stay until removal is confirmed (research line 179 "confirm its state, and cancel"), and must deep-link to the rule's Settings page.
- **S5. Spec contradicts research on the original.** S2 says "The original is cancelled as the proxy path does today." Research line 139 says "The original stays in the shade, or stays snoozed." Pick one per item class (pass-through versus filtered).
- **S6. Define "elected" as one pure function.** S2's "plus per-app and per-category sound election" can be read two ways:
  - as an extra delivery decision that overrides the budget; or
  - as a sound attribute on existing deliveries.
  
  Recommend the second. Also: a batch tick of N elected items should produce at most one audible alert. Every elected alert comes from one package, so Android's cooldown (Android 16 may enable it by default) and Android 16 auto-grouping will soften later ones **(needs device test)**.
- **S7. Work profile.** The owner has one on the Pixel 9a.
  - The personal listener sees work notifications. They will be silenced, and an elected one would republish work content into a personal-profile Farhan notification.
  - Default: never elect work-profile items, and disclose that they go silent.
  - Whether DND is per profile group: **needs device test**.
- **S8. Mock-up claims Farhan can't back.**
  - "Your own DND: off" can't be read while Farhan's rule masks it.
  - "Kept quiet by Farhan" can't be attached to Reddit's notification.
  - "Farhan copies who may call you" changes with M1 to: "Calls ring as they do now".
- **S9. Disclaimer gaps (S7).**
  - Force-stop or an OEM battery kill: the listener does not reconnect until the app is reopened.
  - Locked boot: nothing breaks through before the first unlock.
  - The DND icon is always on, other apps read DND as on, and Wear OS DND sync may mute the watch **(needs device test)**.
- **S10. Add invariant 5:** Farhan never calls `setRingerMode`, `setInterruptionFilter`, `setNotificationPolicy`, `requestInterruptionFilter` or `requestListenerHints` outside the S8 experiment.
  - The ringer did change across the probe's reboot and cleanup (`calls/api35-modes.txt:868`: priorRinger=2 → ringer=1; research line 256).
  - Enforce with a whole-tree ban plus a positive control.
- **S11. Rescue (S9).** The most useful rescue for a stuck mute is removing the rule or revoking DND access, not re-granting. Check whether `cmd notification disallow_dnd <pkg>` deletes the rule.

## NIT

- Intent's "Android keeps and merges the user's state": manual Settings taps were never tested (research lines 152 and 207). Mark it **needs device test**.
- S1 "visible and removable in Android Settings": Android 15 may let the user disable an app mode but not delete it. **Needs device test.**
- The S5 diagnostic snapshot of filter and policy is not needed for the pilot; cut it.

## (2) Architecture and reuse

**Placement:** inside `notification_filter`, because election is coupled to the delivery pipeline.
- `notification_filter_domain/.../sound/` (pure):
  - `MutePolicy` (Farhan's value type, all fields required);
  - `SoundControlState` (Off / Creating / Held / Suspended(reason) / Paused(reason));
  - `Reconciler` (pure: state + observation → actions);
  - `ElectionPolicy`.
- `notification_filter_data/.../sound/` (Android adapters): the rule port, channel, status notifier, receivers, worker. Reuse the BOOT receiver at `NotificationDeliveryReceiver.kt:21`.

**Ports** (needed for testability):

| Port | Covers |
|---|---|
| `ZenRulePort` | add, update, remove, owned rules, rule state, set state, consolidated policy, current filter, policy access; throws a typed `AccessLost` |
| `BreakthroughChannelPort` | create, read bypass and importance |
| `GrantsPort` | the three grants |
| `SoundStateStore` | synchronous commit |
| Clock / boot id | time and reboot detection |

**Serialisation:** one `SoundControlController` serialises all rule mutations behind its own Mutex. Do not nest it in `DeliveryGate`, which says "never nest". The reconciler's action type should have no Create or Activate case; those exist only on the user-action entry point. That makes "never re-enable behind their back" a type rule, not a test.

**S2 proxy reuse holds only partly:**
- `ProxyNotificationPoster.post(item)` has no sound or channel parameter. Today the adapter hard-codes `silent` and reads preferences itself (`NotificationFilterDataModule.kt:58-64`).
- Change it to `post(item, alert: ProxyAlert)` with `ProxyAlert` = {Breakthrough, Normal, Silent}, decided in the domain. Thread `channelId` through `postProxyNotification`.
- Tag `farhan:<id>` / id 1 and tap and action capture carry over unchanged.
- Budget: unchanged if election is only an attribute (S6).

content.text:
The sound-control spec review is back, and its biggest finding changes a decision you made. The review found real problems, which is why the sound-control timeline matters for your APK.

**Your call decision changes.** You approved copying your call settings into Farhan's rule. The reviewer showed that this would make things worse. The only call policy an app can read is the one stored with your regular DND mode, such as starred callers only. Copying that into Farhan's rule would apply it all the time. When your DND is off, a non-starred call would go silent where today it rings. The transcripts show exactly that. The fix is simpler: Farhan's rule always allows calls from anyone, plus repeat callers. Android applies the strictest of the active rules, so with your DND on your own call settings still win. With it off, calls ring as today. I'll set it up that way unless you object.

**Other changes to the spec:**
- **Notifications that go silent:** exceptions, critical notifications and system ones would go silent under the rule, because Farhan doesn't post a loud copy for them. The spec needs an answer for these.
- **Repeat messages:** a second message in a conversation would not sound.
- **Muted with nothing to elect:** if Farhan is switched off or the listener dies, it must release the rule and say so. The reviewer called this the key protection against a stuck mute.
- **Backups and imports:** a restored backup could turn the mute on silently on another phone. That is a database-style bug in the settings export.
- **Rule left behind:** after clear-data or a downgrade, a rule could survive with the feature off. A reboot check handles that.
- **Detail fixes:** the exact Do Not Disturb policy fields, and creating the breakthrough channel only after the DND grant.

**One point I'm disputing:** the reviewer says the loud copy breaks through your own DND too. That was your stated intent, since you asked for sounds that break through DND, so I'm arguing for a disclosure and a later option, not a behaviour change.

**Timeline:** sound control can't responsibly finish inside two hours. The safe version is a smaller first pilot with the rule, the Off control and the loud copy. I've asked the reviewer for the smallest set of fixes that protects against a stuck mute and changed calls. I'll fold the rest in after that.

The combined APK still goes ahead. At about the two-hour mark it includes everything that has passed its gates. Sound control goes in flagged off, or waits for a follow-up. I'll tell you exactly which at that point.

## 1. M2: I accept the downgrade to a disclosure, with two conditions

The owner said "send sounds that break through DND", and you're right that a normal-channel proxy would be intercepted by Farhan's own rule. The bypass channel is the only way an elected alert sounds at all.

What the disclosure doesn't cover:

- **The shipped copy says the opposite.** The mock-up bullet and S7 both say "A stricter Do Not Disturb mode of your own still silences them." With the AOSP default policy (`allowPriorityChannels=true`, `dnd/api35-recovery.txt:26`) that is false. Research line 152 only shows blocking by a mode that denies priority channels. A disclosure can't sit next to a sentence that contradicts it, so that bullet must be replaced, not added to.
- **The owner can't easily switch it off per mode.** Bypass is set per channel and applies to every mode. On Android 15/16 the owner's per-mode control is probably all-or-nothing ("allow priority channels"), which would also silence their other apps' exceptions (needs device test on the Pixel). The disclosure should name the control that does work: turn off "Override Do Not Disturb" on Farhan's breakthrough channel. That stops breakthrough in every mode, including Farhan's own.

Suggested line: "Elected alerts can sound during your own Do Not Disturb and Bedtime modes. To stop that, turn off 'Override Do Not Disturb' for Farhan's alert channel."

The remaining harm is sleep interruption by an elected item at night. The owner can accept that.

## 2. Smallest set for a flagged-off, owner-tested pilot of slices 1–2

One design rule makes most of the list cheap: **the reconciler can only release.** Its action type has no Create or Activate case. Only the enable or resume tap creates or activates the rule.

That one rule takes care of these risks for free:

| Risk | Why it's covered |
|---|---|
| Re-enabling behind the owner's back | Nothing outside a tap can activate the rule. |
| An imported or restored "On" | It finds no rule and cannot create one (M9 risk gone). |
| A rule the user deleted | It is never recreated. |
| A user stop in Settings | No Paused latch or status broadcast needed: Farhan reads the rule's state and shows "Stopped in Settings, tap to resume". |

**Must hold now** (each protects against a stuck mute, changed calls or a rule left behind):

1. **Calls (M1).** Calls from anyone plus repeat callers, as fixed values.
2. **Full policy (M10).** Every ZenPolicy field set explicitly: alarms and media allowed, visual effects all shown, device effects null. Without this, an alarm or media setting inherited from the owner's default could change behaviour.
3. **Orphan cleanup (M6 + M7).** On app start and on listener connect, regardless of the flag: if no persisted On, remove every owned rule found by Farhan's fixed `conditionId`. Adopt by stored id, else by conditionId, never by name.
4. **Persist order (M8, reduced).** `commit()` "desired On, generation" before `addAutomaticZenRule`. Crash windows are then covered by item 3.
5. **Fail-open (M5).** Release the rule when any of these holds:
   - the filter switch or app main switch is off (`NotificationService.kt:240`);
   - any of the three grants is missing;
   - the breakthrough channel reads back without bypass or at importance NONE.
6. **Channel order (M11, reduced).** Create the breakthrough channel only after policy access is granted, and read it back. A bad read-back feeds item 5.
7. **Off.** Persist Off, remove the rule, and keep the status notification until removal is confirmed (S4). If removal fails, the notification links to Modes settings.
8. **No other zen or ringer writes (S10).** A whole-tree ban with a positive control.
9. **Enable key name.** Keep the enable key out of the `notification_experiment_` prefix. It then falls to `Unsupported` and is never exported, with zero catalog code.

**Red tests for this set** (fake `ZenRulePort` and `SoundStateStore`):
- policy fields pinned by name, calls ANY even when the fake readable policy is STARRED;
- flag off with an owned rule present → rule removed;
- stale id → adopted by conditionId, no add;
- a foreign rule is never touched (positive control: the owned rule is removed);
- rule missing while desired On → no add;
- each fail-open precondition → rule released;
- crash between persist and remove → completed on restart;
- the ban test.

**On the emulator:**
- create, then read the policy back;
- competitor stays silent while the proxy alerts;
- a non-starred call rings while held with DND off;
- clear data while held → rule removed on next launch.

**Can wait for slice 3, with a one-line disclosure:**

- **M2:** the line from section 1.
- **M4:** "While muted, only the first message in a conversation sounds until you open or dismiss Farhan's alert."
- **M9 backup and import exclusion:** no disclosure needed, because the release-only reconciler makes it harmless.
- **M11 versioned channel recovery:** "If you turn off Farhan's alert override, Farhan turns sound control off; reinstall to reset it."
- **M5 dead-man alarm:** "If Farhan stops, force-stopped or killed by the system, your phone stays muted until you open Farhan or tap Off in the status notification or Modes settings."
- **S7 work profile:** "Work-profile notifications are silenced too."
- **M3:** see section 3.

## 3. M3: yes, there's a simpler honest answer, and it's safer for the screener

Farhan can't make another app's notification sound natively. So "let the owner pick audible exception apps" inside Farhan would mean building the duplicate after all. The honest version uses Android's own control:

- **At enable**, list the owner's exception apps (from `notification_filter_exceptions`) and say: "These apps, and notifications Farhan marks Critical, will be silent. To keep one audible, allow it in Android's Do Not Disturb app exceptions."
- **No code is needed for this to work.** Farhan's rule allows priority channels, so any channel the owner sets to bypass in Android sounds natively. That keeps its own sound and identity, and it keeps working when Farhan is off.

**The screener comes out better this way.**
- If the screener is part of the default dialer (Pixel Call Screen) or posts with `CATEGORY_CALL`, the call path treats it as a call. With calls from anyone it then behaves exactly as today, untouched.
- A Farhan duplicate is what would put it at risk: it would make a CRITICAL item audible and give it Farhan's identity.
- If duplicates come later, they must be per-app opt-in, with CRITICAL excluded by default.

Needs device tests on the owner's phone:
- whether Android 15/16 lets the user grant bypass to another app's channel from the Modes UI;
- whether the screener's notification passes as a call while Farhan's rule is held.

Verdict on the reduced set: **OK for a flagged-off, owner-tested pilot of slices 1–2**, if items 1–9 and their red tests hold and the disclosures above ship in the enable text.

content.text:
The sound-control spec is settled and Sol is writing its failing tests. The reviewer accepted both of my pushbacks.

**What the reviewer accepted:**
- **Breaking through your own DND is fine** because you asked for it. It becomes a disclosure. The enable screen says elected alerts can sound during your own DND and Bedtime modes. It also names the control that stops it, which is turning off "Override Do Not Disturb" on Farhan's alert channel.
- **Exception apps and critical notifications** stay silent while the rule is held. There's no duplicate-alert machinery in the pilot. If you want one audible, you allow it in Android's own Do Not Disturb app exceptions, and the enable screen lists your exception apps. Your call screener stays untouched. Whether it still passes as a call under Farhan's rule needs a test on your phone.

**The design rule that makes the pilot cheap:** Farhan's background checker may only turn the rule off. Only your tap on enable or resume can create or activate it. That makes these safe by construction:
- nothing re-enables behind your back;
- a restored backup can't turn the mute on;
- a rule you deleted is never recreated;
- a stop in Settings shows as "Stopped in Settings, tap to resume".

**What the pilot guarantees against a stuck mute:**
- Farhan releases the rule when the filter is off, a grant is missing or the alert channel lost its override.
- It cleans up an orphaned rule on app start, even if the feature is off.
- It never touches a rule it doesn't own.

**Four things are in the pilot:**
- Calls from anyone, plus repeat callers.
- A fully specified Do Not Disturb policy.
- A status notification with an Off action.
- The loud copy on a channel created only after the DND grant.

The reviewer judged this OK for a flagged-off pilot you test yourself.

Sol is writing the failing tests now, covering every item in the spec's list plus emulator tests that only need to compile for now. I'll check them on Boat myself. Running in parallel: snooze green, the apps list, this red phase and the testing-strategy planner. Nothing is waiting on you.

# File PR

Before filing, check whether a PR for this branch already exists. Review the
diff locally against the base branch (usually `origin/main`) to make sure its

New threads inherit only the project from context; branch, worktree, and env mode always come from the configured defaults. If model identity is unavailable, name the harness without guessing a model.

Before submission, check the title, description, quotes, and attachments for
secrets and private details.

Open a real PR rather than a draft so review bots run. If `gh pr create` fails
because the GraphQL rate limit is used up, open it through REST with
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls -f title=... -f head=... -f base=... -F body=@<file>`. If the user also asked
to babysit it, continue with the `babysit-pr` skill.

Source: https://github.com/t3dotgg/tstack/blob/main/skills/file-pr/SKILL.md, plus these
owner rules, which win where they conflict:

- **No AI attribution in upstream PRs or commits.** Skip the "Created with <model> in
  <harness>" line and any Co-Authored-By trailer on OpenStrap/* PRs.
- **Approval:** upstream PRs open only with the owner's per-PR approval. Draft the body,
  serve it (tailserve), and wait.
- **Body shape** (blend of this skill and OpenStrap/analytics#99):
  1. Problem in plain words, with the measured cost.
  2. The solution in one or two sentences, with the headline number.
  3. **What a user sees.**
  4. **What changes:** a short bullet list.
  5. `---`-separated sections, bold titles on Benchmarks, Review order and Questions:

     Tests (counts per file set, full suite, skips explained, device line), **Suggested
     review order** (commit by commit, smallest first), Change distribution, Known issues
     kept as on main, **Questions for reviewers**.
- **Easy to review and accept:** one concern per commit with a message that says why;
  a review order that maps to commits; every behavior change pinned by a named test;
  state exactly what output changes (or that none does) and what was not tested.
- **Device line:** "I have run this on my own device: Pixel 9a on Android/GrapheneOS."
  only when the owner has run the same algorithms on the phone.
- Babysit after opening: answer every bot finding with evidence (regression → fix with a
  red test first; pre-existing or false positive → reply with the reason).

content.text:
The testing-strategy report is done. Most of the emulator-only checks can move off the emulator.

**What the emulator is used for today:**
- **25 instrumented tests at the current base:** 6 can run as plain code, and 18 can run in Robolectric, the Android simulator that runs on the computer. They use JSON, SQLite, DataStore, settings storage or Compose. Only one needs a real device. It checks raw component states in Android's package manager.
- **No instrumented test touches notifications:** none uses Android's notification manager, UI automation or a bound listener. Those checks live in the probe scripts and the manual snooze and sound evidence runs, and they stay on the emulator.

**Proven on Boat, not just read:**
- **Migration test:** a Room migration test over the exported schemas passed in 6.2 seconds, and it failed when I renamed a column in the schema. It does catch drift.
- **Screenshot test:** a themed Compose chip row rendered with the app's real font and matched its saved image, and it failed when the theme changed. That took 6.7 seconds.
- **Setup cost:** one extra step is needed so the schemas reach the test (92 KB, debug only).

**Timing:** a warm Robolectric run takes about 52 seconds. A migration check through the emulator takes roughly 3–5 minutes. So each iteration saves about 2–4 minutes. The "20–40 minutes a day" figure is the researcher's guess.

**What it can't replace:** Robolectric's fake notification classes have no snooze, no DND rules, no group cancels and no listener callbacks. Snooze return timing, DND, auto-grouping and performance stay on a real device. To stop the fakes drifting from real Android, one contract test suite runs against both the fake and the emulator occasionally.

**Two refactors would unlock more:**
- Pull the inbox chips out into a screen that takes plain state. They're built inline under Hilt now, so a screenshot test can't reach them.
- Move the four domain files that import Android into another module, so the domain module becomes plain Kotlin that a shared fakes module can use.

**Recommended first slice after the APK:**
- the snooze database migration test, on Robolectric;
- a screenshot test for the apps-list chips;
- contract tests for the snooze platform piece.

The snooze green run keeps using the emulator for its checks, so I'm not changing it mid-run. Everything is in `research/test-strategy-no-emulator.md`. The padding PR is still waiting for your go.

# Update scout-module locks

Use this skill when a change in a satellite repository needs to be reflected in a
phoe-nix scout module's `flake.lock` files.

Before any push, show the user the change and ask for confirmation to push it to
GitHub. Do not infer push approval from approval to edit files or update locks.

After the user confirms:

1. Commit the satellite repository change with a scoped message, then push the
   intended branch to GitHub.
2. Inspect every relevant `flake.nix` in phoe-nix, including the top-level
   `flake.nix` and affected `scout-modules/*/flake.nix` files. Confirm that each
   usage points to the intended fork, repository, and branch. If any reference is
   wrong or ambiguous, stop and ask before updating locks.
3. From the phoe-nix checkout, update the satellite input and all affected scout
   modules. For example, when updating usagewindow and agent-integration:

   cd ~/Documents/repos/phoe-nix
   nix flake update usagewindow
   nix scout update usagewindow agent-integration
   git add scout-modules/*/flake.lock

4. Review the staged lockfile diff. Stage only the affected scout-module lock
   files, verify that no unrelated files changed, and report the exact lockfiles
   updated. Do not commit or push phoe-nix unless the user separately asks for
   that.

Do not update a lock from an unpublished local branch, silently retarget a flake
input, or run a broad lock update when named inputs and modules are sufficient.

nix-scout — scout module switcher

Usage:
  nix-scout list                        List scout modules and their facets
  nix-scout inspect <name>              Evaluate and explain one scout module
  nix-scout new <name> [FACET...]       Scaffold a scout module (facets: scout home baseline flakelet)
  nix-scout build <name...> [NIX-FLAGS] Materialize and build scout outputs without applying them
  nix-scout switch <name...> [NIX-FLAGS] Materialize, build, and apply scout modules (in order)
  nix-scout switch <path>               Install a store path or flake installable into profile
  nix-scout update <name...|all>        Sync module flake.lock(s) with declared inputs
  nix-scout status                      Show active scout profile + gc-roots + flakelet status
  nix-scout clear                       Clear scout profile and gc-roots
  nix-scout doctor                      Check flakelet integration health and print pass/fail report
  nix-scout completions SHELL             Print shell completions (fish, bash, zsh)

NIX-FLAGS are forwarded to 'nix build' (e.g. --show-trace, --option foo bar).
Flags may appear before or after <name>, or after -- for flags that take arguments.

'nix-scout update' first rewrites each flake.nix input URL the module shares
with NIX_SCOUT_PARENT to the host's source and branch (a mismatched URL makes
nix drop the host's lock entry and re-resolve), then syncs a module's
committed flake.lock from NIX_SCOUT_PARENT's
own flake.lock (the same starting point materialize-module.sh already uses
for tmpdir builds at switch time), pruned down via 'nix flake metadata' to
exactly what the module's flake.nix references -- the host's lock is a
superset of what any module needs, and a real 'nix flake' command rewrites a
lock with unreferenced extra nodes in place same as it would add a missing
one, so an unpruned copy would make flakelet's own read-only eval_user hit
the exact permission failure this tool exists to prevent, just from the
opposite direction. A module's own lock is never independently resolved --
it just mirrors the relevant slice of the host's; 'nix-scout new' does the
same at scaffold time. 'switch' runs this sync automatically (non-fatally)
before materializing, so a module that's fallen out of sync with the host is
kept current without a separate manual step.

Facets: a scout module may export any combination of:
  profile     packages.<system>.scout with bin/  — installed into scout nix profile
  home-files  packages.<system>.scout with home-files/ — files copied into $HOME
  activate    packages.<system>.scout with executable activate — runs after
              home-files apply on both 'nix-scout switch' and rebuild activation
  baseline    a NixOS module, imported directly on nixos-rebuild — can set ANY
              system-wide option. Never built/applied by 'nix-scout switch';
              only takes effect on the next rebuild.
  flakelet    flakelets.<attr> — registered with flakelet on rebuild; updated on switch

  Module flake.nix always uses facet separation:
    Every scout module declares inputs.nix-scout and uses mkScoutModule ./. inputs { ... }.
    See README.md for the facet layout (scout / home / baseline / flakelet).
  Empty sections keep the denoting comment. 'nix-scout new' scaffolds this layout.

  switch fan-out: each facet script self-detects and no-ops if its output is absent.
  'switch' never touches 'baseline' — it only takes effect via nixos-rebuild.
  The flakelet entry must exist in /etc/flakelet.json (populated by nixos-rebuild).
  If the entry is missing: rebuild once to register, then retry nix-scout switch.

Home-files removal: files nix-scout applied that later vanish from the config
are handled per policy — remove (default) | keep | keep-if-modified | inform,
declared per file in the module's home-manage.json (or, for Home Manager
files, nix-scout.homeFilePolicies). Only the NixOS rebuild activation deletes;
'switch' never deletes — it reports, for every vanished file, what a rebuild

Snooze pilot, code review round 1 (tier 1). Diff 717faf6..c88fde7, author Sol. Reviewer: Opus.
Read: brief r1, spec v3/v3.1/v3.2, red and green reports, spec reviews r1/r2 and exchange, snooze-android-flexibility, evidence groups/ and groups-hidden-cancel/. No Gradle run; every finding below comes from reading the code paths named, and each cites the lines to check.

SCORE[error-paths]: 4/10 (S1 and S4 lose or leak notifications in common cases; S2 and S3 act against the owner. Fixing S1-S4 with tests through the real coordinator and service would raise it to 8; bar 8)
SCORE[architecture]: 6/10 (W7 rule assumes Farhan cancels summaries, which W7(a) makes false; dead SnoozeTracker, delayUntilNextMoment and SnoozeHandler.onListenerConnected; returns reuse SnoozeInput with MEDIUM placeholders. Fix S2 and delete dead code for 7; bar 7)
SCORE[legibility]: 7/10 (CLAIM tags are mostly sourced. snooze-group-device overclaims, and "funded" in the copy is jargon; bar 7)
SCORE[durability]: 6/10 (charging core is right: W2 order, single-statement row step, NotOwned, stable effectId, recovery via gate. S4 leaves returns uncharged, and a cleared row with a deadline captures its key forever; bar 8)
VERDICT: CHANGES

S1 [blocker] [needed for bar: yes] [class: prod-wiring] [concern: error-paths] NotificationService.kt:386-400, SnoozeHandler.kt:255-258, NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:330, :314, :296-301
Every in-process fallback (everything after onPosted) is cancelled from the shade and never proxied. offerFreshPost calls coordinator.captureEvent(sbn.key), giving order N. When the snooze path takes custody (handled = true), processNotificationPosted returns without coordinator.accept(N): onArrival is the only caller of accept. Later, fallback() cancels the original and calls proxyArrival = onArrival(row, priority) with eventOrder = null, so accept stays a no-op. At each batch tick, deliver() hits `unprocessed(item.id)` (order N > accepted, not removed) and returns Deferred. onBatchTick only pulls nextHead after Delivered, so the stuck row also blocks its app's queue at that priority. This lasts until 4096 newer keys evict the event or the process restarts.
Reproduction: snooze on, defaults. A HIGH post is snoozed. The owner turns snooze off; at the return the budget is exhausted, giving RetryAt and then fallback SNOOZE_OFF. The original disappears, sits in the inbox, and is never delivered. The same happens for NO_FUNDED_MOMENT, DAILY_LIMIT, NATIVE_FAILURE, UNCONFIRMED, NOT_A_RETURN, and BEFORE_DEADLINE (a messaging app updating within ms of the snooze request, which is common). It also covers the W7(b) pending restore. LOST is unaffected because it happens in a new process.
The handler tests miss this because proxyArrival is a fake list. No test drives a fallback through the real coordinator after captureEvent.
Fix: accept the arrival's order when the snooze path takes custody, for example withSnoozeAdmission(order) { ... } marking it accepted when the block returns true. Add a coordinator test: captureEvent(id), take custody via the snooze admission, call onArrival(row) with no order, then onBatchTick posts the row. Mutation check: deleting the accept call must turn it red.

S2 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: consent-bypass] [concern: error-paths] SnoozeHandler.kt:270-273, SnoozeHandler.kt:142-145, NotificationService.kt:424-426, SnoozeHandlerTest.kt:562-600
W7(b) and (c) bring back notifications the source app or the owner removed. W7's premise was "Farhan's own proxy path listener-cancels summaries". But W7(a), at NotificationService.kt:384, means Farhan never cancels a summary while snooze is on. So every reason-12 removal it sees then comes from the app or the user. The device evidence agrees.
- F4 and F5 show snoozed children survive a summary cancel. Android also co-snoozes the summary: summaries 1100, 1200, 1300 and 1510 carry reason 18 and an "until" in groups/T-minus-1m.txt and listener.txt, although Farhan never snoozed them. So (c), restoring a missing grouped row as pending on the same boot, guards a cascade that does not happen. In practice it only fires when the app cancelled a snoozed child.
- F5's refresh of 1511 was triggered by the fixture listener's cancel, which stands in for a Farhan cancel that production no longer performs.
- The case that matters was not run: the source cancels the summary after a child has returned.
Reproduction: snooze on; a grouped chat child returns and is charged. The owner reads the chat; the app cancels its summary, and NMS cascades REASON_GROUP_SUMMARY_CANCELED to the child. refreshProxy then posts a Farhan proxy of the read message. For (c): the owner reads on another device, and the app cancels the snoozed child, which sends no callback. After the deadline plus one tick, the scan restores the row as pending, and the batch path proxies it and charges it. A user swiping the group probably cascades reason 12 the same way; this is unverified.
The tests at 562-600 pin the rule as the spec wrote it.
Fix: treat reason 12 as collateral only for a summary Farhan cancelled. Record the group keys of summaries the proxy path cancels; while snooze is on there are none. Otherwise treat it as SOURCE_APP_CANCELLED (row cleared). Drop (c) and apply the same-boot rule (cleared) to grouped rows. Also null snoozeGroupKey in COMPLETE_SNOOZE_RETURN, or bound its life, so a delivered row does not stay "grouped" forever. Rewrite the three tests, and add one where the app cancels the summary.

S3 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: consent-bypass] [concern: error-paths] NotificationService.kt:325
returnInput.filterEnabled reads isNotificationServiceStatsEnabled() and ignores the app main switch. Elsewhere the filter is off when preferences.isServiceEnabled() is false (stats AND app_main_switch): see processNotificationPosted via ServiceUtilImpl.isNotificationServiceEnabled, and NotificationDeliveryEngine.kt:18 and :23.
Reproduction: the owner pauses Farhan with the main switch while items are snoozed. A return arrives, and settle still decides by budget: it charges it, re-snoozes it (hiding it again while Farhan is paused), or falls back. A fallback cancels the original and queues a proxy that the paused batch tick never posts. W5 says filter off means release: leave it visible, close the row, no charge.
The handler test at :504 passes filterEnabled = false directly, so the wrong source is untested.
Fix: build the input from isServiceEnabled() (resolve it before the call, since it is suspend). Add a service-level or seam test that the main switch off releases a return.

S4 [blocker] [needed for bar: yes] [class: hidden-state] [concern: durability] NotificationService.kt:355-359, SnoozeHandler.kt:166-169, NotificationDao.kt:71 (markNotificationAsCleared), NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:262
Clearing a snoozed row from the inbox breaks I2 for that return and captures its key forever. Spec review r2 raised this as S9, and v3.2 never decided it. MarkNotificationAsCleared calls clearInbox, which sets isCleared = 1 and leaves snoozeDeadline set. At the return, settle finds isCleared and returns false: the original stays visible, beeps, is uncharged and is not in the inbox. Worse, the processNotificationPosted pre-check (`find(id)?.snoozeDeadline != null`, then settle, then return) catches every later post of that key. Messaging apps reuse one key per conversation, so after one swipe in Farhan's inbox the conversation bypasses the filter permanently: never stored, proxied, snoozed or charged.
Reproduction: snooze on; a chat message is snoozed; the owner swipes it away in Farhan's inbox (or clears all). It returns visible and uncharged, and every later message in that chat shows unfiltered.
Fix:
- The pre-check uses the live predicate (deadline != null AND not cleared AND not delivered), the same one as liveSnoozes.
- An owned cleared row at return: cancelVisible, null the snooze columns, record REMOVED, return true.
- The inbox clear path closes custody, so the row cannot keep a deadline after it is cleared.
- Tests: clear while snoozed, then return, giving an original cancelled with no charge; then a fresh post of the same key goes through the normal path.

- NotificationService.kt:391 alreadyDelivered = isDelivered ignores isCleared. A chat whose returned original was dismissed takes the proxy path for its next message (ALREADY_DELIVERED) instead of snooze. Use isDelivered && !isCleared.

SnoozeTrackerTest and the delay-only cases in SnoozeTimingTest pin dead code ("pins dead code" mode). - NotificationService.kt:349 the previous-tick formula in reconcileSnoozes, (minute % interval + interval), is untested. A mutation to minute % interval would stay green.
- NotificationService.kt:318-333 returnInput fabricates packageName "" and a MEDIUM priority, setting and flags to satisfy SnoozeInput for settle. Give settle a small input of its own (filterEnabled, snoozeEnabled, now, zone, testingMode).
- SnoozeHandler.kt:153 repeats the summary check already made at NotificationService.kt:384.
- NotificationService.kt:387 a post that is no longer current returns handled = true and still runs captureActions(), which retains actions for a key with no row.
- NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:236 the outer catch maps a store read failure to NoFundedMoment, so the fallback event is mislabelled. The spend timestamp uses the handler's now, not environment.timeContext (V4 asks for one clock).
- NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:319-323 the batch reservation adds points for reserved returns whose priority is IGNORING, which is conservative. hasSnoozeCapacity does the same for owned rows.
- AutomationSettingsSection.kt: "no funded time in the next 48 hours" is jargon (try "no time with budget left in the next 48 hours"). Counters omit FAILED and LOST. A return fallback is labelled "could not snooze". v3.1 asked the copy to say the daily retry limit resets when Farhan restarts.
- NotificationService.kt:393 CLAIM(snooze-group-device) says the "collateral cases" passed. F5's collateral cancel came from a fixture listener, and the returned-child source-cancel case was not run.

HARDENING-STASH:
- NotificationService.kt:121-123 drainSnoozeReturns runs inside the same try as the work item. If a settle throws (for example a DB error), the current Posted or Removed work is dropped, and that repeats while the flag stays set.
- SnoozeHandler.kt:250-253, :217 release() and the retry upsert are read-modify-write of the whole row outside DeliveryGate. A concurrent clearInbox or markCleared under the gate can be overwritten (isCleared reset).
- SnoozeHandler.kt:135-141 an unconfirmed snooze is only detected after its deadline (W3 as written). A silent native no-op leaves the original visible and uncharged for up to 48 h.
- NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:278-281 the batch path reserves only returns due at this tick. Proxy deliveries at 09:00 can spend points promised to 10:00 or 11:00 returns, which are then denied with a beep (W4 as written).
- A post that races the snooze request (app update within ms) gives a BEFORE_DEADLINE fallback while Android has already hidden the updated record. That yields a proxy now plus the original at its deadline, refreshed without charge. Visible twice, charged once.
- An owner's own shade snooze of a returned, charged notification comes back as an update of a delivered row and is replaced by a silent proxy.

- It proves: children snooze and return with summaries present (F1-F3); Android co-snoozes the summary itself, so W7(a) holds; snoozed children survive a summary cancel by the source (F4) or by a listener (F5); a listener cancel cascades reason 12 to an active returned child (F5); ungrouped auto-group summaries are not proxied (F6); returns can beep (F7, only some).
- It does not prove: that any reason-12 event reaches Farhan from its own cancel while snooze is on (it cannot); the source-cancels-summary-after-return case (S2); any fallback path delivering a proxy (S1). F5's refresh shows the resurrection mechanism, not a protected case.

Wiring check: every new port has a production implementation in NotificationService or NotificationFilterDataModule (SnoozePlatform, SnoozeLedger, SnoozeReturnBudget, scheduleAt, completeSnoozeReturn, liveSnoozes). Orchestrator reply to your round-1 snooze review (argument exchange; read-only, edit nothing, no git writes, never vigil orchestrator mode). I checked S1 myself: NotificationService.kt:386-400 returns without coordinator.accept(order); the fallback's onArrival(eventOrder=null) makes accept a no-op, so unprocessed() stays true and deliver() returns Deferred. Agreed, blocker. S3 and S4 I accept too. Where I push back or want your position:

1. S4 scope. Your fix has three parts: (a) live predicate (deadline != null AND not cleared AND not delivered) in the pre-check, (b) settle on an owned cleared row = cancelVisible + null snooze columns + REMOVED, (c) the inbox clear path closes custody. A separate branch (fix/clear-per-category, review-complete, merging into this build) rewrites markNotificationAsCleared and the clear paths, so (c) adds a merge conflict and a second place that must know about snooze. Does (a)+(b) alone close the hole? I think yes: once the pre-check uses the live predicate, a cleared row with a stale deadline cannot capture the key, and (b) disposes of the row at its return. Name any state where (a)+(b) still leaves a row that bypasses the filter or is never charged or closed. If you can name one, I do (c); if not, we skip (c).
2. S2. I accept dropping W7(c) (the same-boot restore of a missing grouped row) and applying the plain cleared rule to grouped rows. For W7(b) I accept "reason 12 is collateral only for a summary Farhan cancelled", with Farhan recording which summary group keys it cancelled. Question: with snooze on, can Farhan's own cancel of a child (fallback or proxy path) make Android cancel an auto-group or app summary and cascade reason 12 to the OTHER returned children? If yes, those are Farhan-caused and should refresh; if no, the recorded set is always empty and I will delete the machinery, not just the rule. What does your device evidence (groups/ F4, F5, F6) say?
3. S1 fix shape. I plan to mark the arrival's order accepted inside withSnoozeAdmission when the block returns true. Is that safe when a NEWER event for the same key (higher order) arrives while custody is held? I expect yes, because accept sets accepted=order of THIS event only, so the newer one stays unprocessed until it runs. Check that, and say if you would rather the handler call accept at the fallback instead.
4. Dead code. I will delete SnoozeTracker, delayUntilNextMoment and onListenerConnected with their tests. Then the green report's re-recorded-key mutation proves nothing; I will ask for one replacement mutation on a production-routed piece (the previous-tick formula in reconcileSnoozes, which you say is untested, plus a test that fails when it becomes minute % interval). Agree?
5. Hardening stash. I plan to decline for the pilot: unconfirmed snooze detected only after the deadline (fail-open: the owner sees the original, nothing lost), DST hour merge, batch reservation of promised points. Object only if you think one of them loses or leaks a notification in a common case.
Answer each numbered point in a few lines, then say whether, with S1-S4 fixed as above plus tests through the real coordinator and service, error-paths reaches 8. Write your reply to /home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/snooze/research/review/snooze-round1-exchange.md

content.text:
Snooze review round 1 gave a CHANGES verdict, and I've sent the reviewer my counter-arguments.

**What the review found:** two blockers and two should-fix items.
- **S1 (blocker):** when snooze takes custody of a post and the item later falls back to the normal path, it is cancelled from the shade and never delivered. This is easy to hit: turning snooze off while items are snoozed, or an app updating within milliseconds of the snooze request. I checked this in the code (`NotificationService.kt:386-400` and `NotificationDeliveryCoordinator.kt:185`) and it is real.
- **S4 (blocker):** clearing a snoozed row in the inbox leaves its snooze deadline set. At the return it is uncharged and beeps. Because chat apps reuse one key per conversation, later messages from that chat then bypass the filter.
- **S2 and S3 (should-fix):**
  - Snooze brings back notifications the app or the owner removed.
  - The return check ignores the app's main on/off switch.

**My position in the argument:**
- I accept S1, S3 and S4.
- On S4, I asked whether the pre-check and return-time fixes are enough, without also changing the inbox clear path. A separate clear-category branch already rewrites that path, and touching it here adds a merge conflict.
- On S2, I accept dropping the same-boot restore of grouped rows. I asked whether Farhan's own cancel can cascade to other returned children. If it can't, I'll delete that machinery.
- I'll delete the dead tracker code. That makes the green report's re-recorded-key mutation meaningless, so I asked for a replacement mutation on code that production uses.
- I'm declining the hardening items for the pilot: an unconfirmed snooze is only noticed after its deadline, the daylight-saving hour merge, and the batch reservation of promised points. They don't lose notifications in common cases.

The reply is due in `research/review/snooze-round1-exchange.md`. After that, the fixes go to Sol with failing tests first. Round 2 with Fable follows, then your OK. I still owe 2–3 mutation checks of my own on the snooze code.

Error-paths reaches 8 once S1–S4 are fixed with tests through the real coordinator and service, but two of the fixes as you described them each miss a second site. Without those, the same bugs stay reachable and it stays at 6. The full reply is in `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/snooze/research/review/snooze-round1-exchange.md`. I edited nothing else and made no git writes.

1. **S4 scope:** skip (c), but (a)+(b) as written don't close the hole.
   - **Second pre-check:** `SnoozeHandler.kt:154` uses the same wrong check (`snoozeDeadline != null`) as the service pre-check. With only the service fixed, the key is still captured while snooze is on.
   - **(b) depends on the in-memory owned entry:** the next scan drops cleared rows from that cache, and so does a restart. Any deadline more than one tick away hits this. The return then comes in as a new arrival and gets snoozed again, which un-clears the row and reverses the owner's clear.
   - **Fix:** decide from the row instead. A cleared row with a deadline, posted at or after that deadline, is a return the owner cleared: cancel the visible original, null the snooze columns, record REMOVED. The evidence shows Android's return post time always lands at or after the stored deadline.
   - **What's left:** a deleted row comes back as a new arrival and is charged once; fine for the pilot. A cleared row whose snoozed record the app cancelled keeps a stale deadline. To close a narrow window where a genuinely new post of that key would be cancelled, have the scan clean those rows too.

2. **S2:** keep the recording machinery, but make it small.
   - **Evidence:** every reason-12 removal in the device logs comes straight after a summary cancel (reason 8 from the app, reason 10 from the test listener). None follows a child cancel. No fallback ran, so the logs have no case of Farhan cancelling a child with siblings present.
   - **Snooze on:** no reason 12 is ever Farhan-caused. Farhan never cancels a summary then, and that includes Android's auto-group summaries.
   - **Snooze turned off:** the proxy path cancels app summaries on arrival (`NotificationService.kt:403`). That cascades reason 12 to children that returned earlier and are still visible originals. So the set isn't always empty: record only at that one cancel site, and only for summaries.
   - **Supporting evidence:** in the hidden-cancel run, the app's own summary cancel cascaded reason 12 to an active sibling. Had that sibling been a returned child, the current code would have re-posted it.

3. **S1 fix shape:** accepting at admission is safe. `accept` sets only this event's order, so a newer event or removal for the same key stays unprocessed until it runs. Don't move it to the fallback: the fallback doesn't know the original order and could accept a newer, unprocessed event. You also need it at a second site: the custody pre-check (`NotificationService.kt:355-359`) returns without accepting its own order. A BEFORE_DEADLINE fallback from that path gets stuck the same way.

4. **Dead code:** agree. Pull the previous-tick formula out of `reconcileSnoozes` into a pure function and pin literal times:
   - 10:25 gives 09:00;
   - 10:00:30 gives 09:00;
   - testing mode at 10:25 gives 10:21;
   - a +05:30 zone at local 10:25 gives local 09:00.

   Changing it to `minute % interval` turns the 10:00:30 case red. Deleting the accept call (S1) and reading the filter flag from stats (S3) also count as mutations through the production path.

5. **Hardening stash:** no objection to declining all three. One unlisted item deserves a two-line fix: the return drain runs inside the same try as each work item (`NotificationService.kt:121-123`). A settle that keeps throwing drops the current post or removal every time. Give the drain its own try/catch.

Read first: `research/review/snooze-round1-reply.txt` (findings S1-S4, stashes) and `research/review/snooze-round1-exchange.md` (reviewer's answers to my pushback). This brief decides what to do. Run Gradle on Boat: `flock /tmp/farhan-boat.lock python3 -I /home/mini/Documents/repos/edge.research/bin/boat-run --sandbox bx_bngcafgz --shell 'nix develop -c' --name <unique> --large <worktree> -- ./gradlew <tasks> --no-daemon -q` (Boat is NOT out of credit; the earlier 0% advisory was wrong).

Intent: a snoozed notification is never lost, never leaks past the filter, and never comes back after the owner or the source app removed it.

## Order of work (red first, one commit per step)

Step 0 (tests, expected RED): add the tests listed under each fix, through the real `NotificationDeliveryCoordinator` and the real service seam, not a fake `proxyArrival` list. Run them; commit red with `# why/catches` on each. Report which are red and why before fixing.
Step 1 (fixes, green): fix in the order S1, S4, S3, S2, then cleanup. Commit per fix.

## S1 (blocker): custody must accept its own event order

- In `withSnoozeAdmission`, when the block returns `true` (snooze took custody), mark THIS event's order accepted (`accept(id, order)` sets only that order). Pass the order into the admission call.
- Also at the second site: the custody pre-check at `NotificationService.kt` ~355-359 returns without accepting its own order; apply the same accept there. A `BEFORE_DEADLINE` fallback from that path is stuck the same way today.
- Do NOT accept at the fallback (it does not know the original order and could accept a newer unprocessed event).
- Tests (real coordinator): captureEvent(id) -> take custody -> fallback `onArrival(row)` with no order -> `onBatchTick` posts the row. Same for the pre-check path. A newer event for the same key stays unprocessed until it runs.
- Mutation: deleting the accept call must turn the test red.

## S4 (blocker): clearing a snoozed row

- Decide from the ROW, not the in-memory owned entry. A cleared row with a snooze deadline, posted at or after that deadline, is a return the owner cleared: cancel the visible original, null the snooze columns (one statement, as COMPLETE_SNOOZE_RETURN does), record REMOVED, return handled.
- The live predicate (deadline != null AND not cleared AND not delivered) goes in BOTH pre-checks: `NotificationService.kt:355-359` and `SnoozeHandler.kt:154`. Move `liveSnoozes` into `NotificationQueries` and use the same predicate, and make it exclude `deliveryInvalidated`; test it against SQLite.
- The reconcile scan cleans cleared rows whose snoozed record the app cancelled (stale deadline), so a genuinely new post of that key is not cancelled later.
- Do NOT change the inbox clear path (the clear-category branch rewrites it; we merge it into the same build).
- Tests: clear while snoozed, then return -> original cancelled, no charge; the next post of that key takes the normal path and is not captured. Also: clear while snoozed, then a scan tick drops the owned entry, then the return arrives (restart variant): same result, not re-snoozed, row stays cleared.

## S3: main switch

- `returnInput.filterEnabled` must come from `isServiceEnabled()` (stats AND app main switch), resolved before the call (it is suspend). Test through the service seam: main switch off + a return -> released, no charge, no re-snooze.
- Mutation: read the stats flag again -> red.

## S2: removals the source or owner made

- Reason 12 (`REASON_GROUP_SUMMARY_CANCELED`) is collateral ONLY for a summary Farhan cancelled. With snooze on Farhan cancels no summary. Record group keys at ONE site: the proxy path's summary cancel (`NotificationService.kt` ~403, snooze turned off). Keep the recorded set small and bounded.
- Anything else is SOURCE_APP_CANCELLED (row cleared). Drop W7(c) (same-boot restore of a grouped row): grouped rows follow the same rule as ungrouped. Null `snoozeGroupKey` in `COMPLETE_SNOOZE_RETURN` (or bound its life).
- Rewrite the three tests at `SnoozeHandlerTest.kt:562-600` that pin the old rule. Add: the app cancels a summary after a child returned and was charged -> no proxy refresh of the child.

## Cleanup and small items

- Delete `SnoozeTracker.kt`, `SnoozeTrackerTest`, `SnoozeTiming.delayUntilNextMoment` and its delay-only tests, `SnoozeHandler.onListenerConnected`, and CLAIM(snooze-tracker-bound). Narrow CLAIM(snooze-group-device) to "grouped children return with their summary [F1-F3, F5 hidden-child]".
- Pull the previous-tick formula out of `reconcileSnoozes` into a pure function; pin literal times: 10:25 -> 09:00; 10:00:30 -> 09:00; testing mode at 10:25 -> 10:21; a +05:30 zone at local 10:25 -> local 09:00. Replacing it with `minute % interval` must turn the 10:00:30 case red.
- `drainSnoozeReturns` gets its own try/catch (a settle that keeps throwing must not drop the current post or removal each time).
- `alreadyDelivered` uses `isDelivered && !isCleared`.
- A post that is no longer current returns handled = true but still runs `captureActions()` (retains actions for a key with no row): skip capture.
- Give `settle` a small input of its own (filterEnabled, snoozeEnabled, now, zone, testingMode) instead of fabricating `packageName ""` and a MEDIUM priority. Drop the repeated summary check at `SnoozeHandler.kt:153`.
- Copy: "no funded time in the next 48 hours" -> "no time with budget left in the next 48 hours"; add FAILED and LOST to the counters; say the daily retry limit resets when Farhan restarts.
- DECLINED for the pilot (do not do): unconfirmed snooze noticed only after the deadline; DST fall-back hour merge; batch reservation of promised points; the whole-row read-modify-write outside DeliveryGate.

## Evidence for the report (`research/snooze-round1-fix-report.md`)

Red list with failing assertion lines; per-fix commit; targeted JVM test counts on domain/data/presentation; `:app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin` and `:app:assembleDebug`; the Room 7->8 migration test still passes; mutation list (S1 accept deleted, S3 flag source, previous-tick formula, live predicate) with red results; anything you disagreed with and why; any edit to an existing test and why.

# build-loop reference: UI work (briefs, inheritance, fidelity)

Source: edge alarms/timelines pilot (owner, 2026-11-19, m233). The implementer had the signed-off
mock-ups but rebuilt toggles, list rows, chart annotations and the hypnogram from scratch. The app
and two earlier pilots already did all of these correctly. The owner caught it from screenshots.

## The rule

UI work inherits before it builds. A UI brief names every source the screen inherits from, and
the implementer reuses that code. New code covers only what the mock-up adds.

## The brief (checked by `scripts/ui-brief-check`)

Any brief that creates or changes a screen, widget, chart or page is a UI brief. Write it to a
file and run `ui-brief-check <brief.md>` before delegating; it exits 1 until the brief has:

```
## UI inheritance
| Source | Path or SHA | Take from it |
|---|---|---|
| Mock-up (signed off) | mockups/…/x-v22.html | layout, copy, order, sizes |
| Original screen | lib/…/alarm.dart @ <sha> | toggles, rows, buttons, theme |
| Prior pilot / landed feature | pilot/day-timeline @ c6b764aae | annotations, list, day row |

## Fidelity check
Screenshot pairs (mock-up | build), same viewport: <dir>
```

- **Mock-up:** the signed-off version, never an earlier one. Read its CSS for sizes and colours.
- **Original screen:** the screen this replaces or extends, at the base SHA.
- **Prior pilots and landed features:** search for them; don't rely on memory. `git branch -a
  | grep -i pilot`, and `git log --all -i --grep=<feature>` for each control the mock-up shows
  (chart, toggle, list row, editor). Name each one, or write `none found: <what you searched>`.
- **Take from it:** the concrete widgets, painters or styles to reuse.

## Implementer duties

1. Before writing UI code, list in the report which widget or painter from each source it will
   reuse. If it won't reuse one, it says why.
2. Never theme around the app: no local `ThemeData`/colour-scheme overrides that change how shared
   controls draw.
3. Before handing back, it takes screenshots of the mock-up and the build at the same viewport,
   puts each pair side by side, and lists every visible difference. That covers layout, order,
   controls, copy, colours, chart marks, and the default state on open. Fix the differences or
   list them as deferred.
4. If the mock-up can't be rendered (no browser), say so, and compare against its CSS and markup
   line by line.

## Gate before the owner sees it

A UI handoff (screenshots, iteration build, APK) is blocked until a fidelity pass has run. A
different model from the author compares the screenshot pairs against the mock-up and the
inheritance table, and writes `fidelity-review.md`. It ranks differences by how much the owner
would notice. Fix the top ones before the owner looks. The orchestrator compares at least one pair
itself, and never forwards screenshots it hasn't compared.

Spec edge 3 and E13 (snooze-pilot-spec.md:55, :94; flexibility doc row "same-key update while timed snooze is pending can remain hidden") say Android absorbs a same-key update into the snoozed record with no callback, and returns the updated record at the deadline. Farhan never sees that update. With the S4 fix the return is then cancelled because the row is cleared: the new message is never shown, never stored and never proxied. Before the fix the return stayed visible, so this loss is new.
Reproduction: snooze on; chat message A is snoozed until the next HIGH tick; the owner swipes A away in Farhan's inbox (MarkNotificationAsCleared); ten minutes later the same conversation sends B, which the app posts under the same key; at the deadline Android returns A+B and Farhan cancels it. Per-row clear followed by a follow-up in the same chat inside the snooze window is ordinary chat use, and for MEDIUM and LOW the window is hours.
The tests pin the blind cancel (the cleared-return cases assert cancel without looking at content).
Fix: do not cancel a cleared return whose content differs from the stored row. One platform read of the active record's title and text (or the Posted fields where they exist) is enough: same as the row means the cleared return, dispose as now; different means a new arrival, so close the custody columns and let it take the normal path (handleStoredPost returns false; on the owned Return path the cheapest pilot option is to close custody and leave it visible). Test: clear while snoozed, return with changed text, assert no cancel and that the post is charged, snoozed or proxied.

Check 5, deletions: no production reference to SnoozeTracker, delayUntilNextMoment, hasOwnedRows or the handler's onListenerConnected remains; the handler tests that used onListenerConnected now drive onBatchTick, which is the production entry. No hollow test found. Note, not a finding: the whole of SnoozeTimingTest went, including the DST, zone and testing-mode alignment cases; SnoozeFundedMomentTest and SnoozePolicyTest still exercise ticks() through nextDeliverableMoment, in UTC only.

Check 6, other new-loss paths looked at and cleared: the new deliveryInvalidated exclusion cannot strand a snoozed row (snooze rows carry sourceEventOrder 0, which INVALIDATE never matches); a summary left alone under snooze stays visible, so its unaccepted order loses nothing; a settle that throws keeps its flag and is retried by the next drain; a full mailbox still processes a native removal under the lock; flagIfOwned refusing an early post sends it to the stored pre-check, which falls back to the proxy path with its order accepted.

Stop recommendation after S5: one small change plus one test. It needs a diff-only look at that change, not another full round; nothing else in this diff blocks the pilot.

Is title+text enough to catch a follow-up in a chat, and what do you do with the false-equal case (an app re-posting identical text, for example 'You have 1 new message')? I would accept cancelling that as the cleared return, because the owner just dismissed the same words. (2) Different content: you say handleStoredPost returns false on the stored path but 'cheapest pilot option: close custody and leave it visible' on the owned path. I would rather have one rule for both paths: close the custody columns in the same guarded statement and let the post take the NORMAL arrival path (settle returns 'not handled'), so B is stored, un-cleared, proxied or queued by its priority and charged like any arrival, and A's old cleared row is simply replaced by B's row (same key). Leaving it visible would beep once, store nothing and not charge, which is the old S4 symptom for B. Can the owned Return path in NotificationService actually fall through to the normal path from there without double handling (the order accepted, the pre-check, the admission lock), or is there a reason it must stay a special case? Read the code; do not answer from memory. (3) The content read: you say one platform read of the active record. Which call do you mean (activeNotifications by key, or the Posted fields the listener callback already carries on the owned path)? Fable's round 2 review of the snooze fixes is back with one new finding, and I'm arguing it with them now.

- **Result:** CHANGES. Fable confirms the four round-1 fixes are done properly. The new finding is one real loss that my own S4 fix introduced.
- **The loss:** if you swipe a snoozed chat message away in the inbox and the same conversation sends a follow-up before the snooze ends, Android quietly merges the follow-up into the hidden notification. When it returns, the fix cancels it as your cleared message, and the follow-up is never shown. That is ordinary chat use.
- **Proposed fix:** compare the returned title and text with the stored row. If they differ, treat it as a new arrival.

First exchange sent. I proposed one rule for both code paths: close the snooze record and let the post take the normal arrival path, rather than leave it visible. I also asked what happens when an app re-posts identical text and what exactly gets compared.

The review ledger wants architecture and legibility scores too, so I'll ask Fable for them in the second exchange. Still waiting on the combined Boat run and Sol's sound-control report.
